title: Fix stale CameraDaemon watchdog cleanup on reinstall
description:
## Problem
After app reinstall, stale daemon watchdog scripts survive because `pkill`/`killall` is unreliable on BYD toybox (documented in AGENTS.md). The old watchdog respawns `app_process` with a `CLASSPATH` pointing to the deleted old APK, causing `ClassNotFoundException: net.bladewatch.app.daemon.CameraDaemon` and `SIGABRT` crashes (3 tombstones in logcat).

## Evidence
```
F/DEBUG: Abort message: 'No pending exception expected: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: net.bladewatch.app.daemon.CameraDaemon
```
Healthy daemon (PID 11386) runs alongside 3 crash tombstones from stale PIDs 16557/16620/16729.

## Fix
Replace `pkill -9 -f 'start_cam_daemon'` / `pkill -9 -f 'byd_cam_daemon'` / `killall` in `DaemonLauncher.kt:191-200` with PID-based enumeration:
```
ps -A -o PID,ARGS | grep ... | awk '{print $1}' | xargs kill -9
```
This must target:
- `start_cam_daemon` watchdog processes
- `start_acc_sentry` watchdog processes
- `byd_cam_daemon` (CameraDaemon)
- `sentry_daemon` (SentryDaemon)
- `acc_sentry_daemon` (AccSentryDaemon)

## Acceptance
- [ ] Clean reinstall no longer produces `ClassNotFoundException: CameraDaemon` tombstones
- [ ] Only one CameraDaemon instance runs after reinstall
- [ ] SentryDaemon and AccSentryDaemon are properly restarted after reinstall
acceptance_criteria: Verify clean reinstall produces zero stale daemon crash tombstones
close_reason: Fix implemented: PID-based kill enumeration replaces pkill/killall; LocationStarterActivity method removed

title: ConnectDispatcher: accept unary content-type application/json (fix 415 on every RPC)
description:
## Problem
The native Android UI cannot reach the daemon over Connect. ConnectDispatcher.dispatch() rejects any request whose Content-Type does not start with "application/connect+json" (HTTP 415). But that is the STREAMING content type. Unary Connect RPCs use "application/json". connect-kotlin 0.6.0 (com.connectrpc.impl.ProtocolClient) sends "application/" + codec.encodingName() => application/json for unary, and "application/connect+" + codec.encodingName() for streaming. Every Android UI call is unary, so 100% of RPCs get 415 before any handler runs.

## File to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java
  - Constant CONTENT_TYPE_CONNECT (~line 37)
  - Content-Type guard (~lines 85-89): if (contentType == null || !contentType.startsWith(CONTENT_TYPE_CONNECT)) -> 415

## Steps
1. Read ConnectDispatcher.java fully first.
2. Replace the strict guard so it ACCEPTS unary "application/json" AND streaming "application/connect+json" (case-insensitive, allow charset suffix e.g. "application/json; charset=utf-8"). Optionally also accept application/proto / application/connect+proto for future binary, but JSON is what is used today.
3. Keep returning 415 only for genuinely unsupported types (e.g. text/html, missing).
4. Do NOT remove the Connect-Protocol-Version: 1 header check or the POST-only check.

## Constraints
- Do not touch the REST handlers or the proto files.
- Do not change AuthMiddleware.
- Response content-type echo is handled in a SEPARATE task (do not change response writing here beyond what is needed to compile).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] POST /bladewatch.v1.VehicleService/GetState with Content-Type: application/json and Connect-Protocol-Version: 1 reaches the handler (no 415).
- [ ] POST with Content-Type: application/connect+json still works (streaming form still accepted).
- [ ] POST with Content-Type: text/html still returns 415.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes.
- [ ] On device (192.168.0.251:5555): open the app, exercise Vehicle/Trips/Recording screens, and confirm logcat no longer shows 415 on /bladewatch.v1.* and data populates.

Do not make mistakes. Read ConnectDispatcher.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: ConnectDispatcher now accepts unary application/json (and streaming application/connect+json) via isSupportedContentType(); tolerant of charset suffix + case. Verified by ConnectContentTypeNegotiationTest (10/10 green): unary request reaches handler (was 415 pre-fix). compileDebugJavaWithJavac BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

title: ConnectDispatcher: echo response Content-Type matching the request (unary application/json) for connect-web/Angular
description:
## Problem
ConnectDispatcher always writes responses with Content-Type: application/connect+json (sendConnectSuccess ~line 127 and the error path ~line 145). For a UNARY request the Connect protocol requires the response Content-Type to match the request (application/json). connect-kotlin 0.6.0 is lenient on the unary response (it branches on HTTP status, not response content-type), but @connectrpc/connect-web v2 (used by the Angular app in web/) validates the unary response content-type and will reject application/connect+json. So even after the request-side fix, the Angular client stays broken.

## File to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java
  - sendConnectSuccess(...) (~line 106 / response headers ~lines 127, 143-148)
  - sendConnectError(...) (~line 145)

## Steps
1. Read ConnectDispatcher.java fully first.
2. Determine unary vs streaming from the REQUEST content-type (passed into dispatch): a request of application/json is unary; application/connect+json is streaming.
3. Thread that classification into sendConnectSuccess/sendConnectError (e.g. a boolean unary flag or pass the negotiated response content-type) and set the response Content-Type accordingly: application/json for unary, application/connect+json for streaming.
4. Keep HTTP status mapping (connectCodeToHttpStatus) and the error JSON body shape unchanged.

## Constraints
- Depends on the request-accept task being merged/coordinated (same file).
- Do not change proto, REST handlers, or AuthMiddleware.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A unary request (Content-Type: application/json) gets a response with Content-Type: application/json.
- [ ] A streaming-form request (application/connect+json) gets application/connect+json back.
- [ ] Error responses echo the same content-type as the corresponding request type.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes.
- [ ] Angular web app (served from the daemon) can perform a real Connect call (e.g. SystemService/GetStatus) without an "unexpected content-type" error.

Do not make mistakes. Read ConnectDispatcher.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: sendConnectSuccess/sendConnectError now take a negotiated content type; responseContentType() echoes application/json for unary, application/connect+json for streaming, defaults to unary json for early errors. Verified by ConnectContentTypeNegotiationTest round-trip (response Content-Type echo asserted for both forms).

title: gRPC/Connect Android UI outage: unary content-type negotiation + hardening
description:
Umbrella for fixing the post-migration regression where the native Android UI (and the Angular web app) cannot reach the daemon over Connect. Root cause: ConnectDispatcher requires the STREAMING content type (application/connect+json) but unary Connect clients (connect-kotlin 0.6.0 and @connectrpc/connect-web v2) send application/json for unary RPCs, so every unary call is rejected with HTTP 415 before the handler runs. Before the migration everything worked over REST.

Evidence:
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java: CONTENT_TYPE_CONNECT = "application/connect+json" (~line 37); request rejected with 415 if Content-Type does not start with it (~lines 85-89); success/error responses always sent as application/connect+json (~lines 127, 145).
- connect-kotlin 0.6.0 com.connectrpc.impl.ProtocolClient bytecode: unary() builds content type as "application/" + codec.encodingName() => application/json; stream() builds "application/connect+" + codec.encodingName() => application/connect+json.
- All Android UI clients use the unary path (ConnectClientProvider -> *ServiceClient -> suspend unary): VehicleClient.kt, TripsClient.kt, RecordingSettingsClient.kt, SurveillanceSettingsClient.kt, LiveStreamClient.kt.
- web/package.json uses @connectrpc/connect-web v2 (same unary application/json behavior).
- ConnectWireParityTest only checks JSON serialization shape, never the HTTP round-trip, so it did not catch this.

Child tasks cover: the core dispatcher fix (request accept + response echo), an HTTP round-trip test, and several lower-severity hardening items surfaced during review. See child issues for detail.
close_reason: All 7 child tasks complete. P0 outage fixed (ConnectDispatcher accepts unary application/json + echoes matching response content-type), proven by ConnectContentTypeNegotiationTest. Hardening done: runBlocking off-main audit (no bug; StrictMode guard added), descriptor-derived surveillance toggle completeness, REST->proto parity tests extended (+8), recording-mode raw-HTTP bypass replaced with SetRecordingMode RPC. Full build + unit tests + assembleDebug green.

title: Surveillance GetStatus: nested {success,status:{...}} vs flat proto -> empty response
description:
Epic: BladeWatch-86a. HIGH IMPACT (surveillance status response is effectively empty over Connect).

PROBLEM: REST sendSurveillanceStatus emits a NESTED {success:true, status:{ initialized, enabled, active, recording, frameCount, ... }} object. The proto GetSurveillanceStatusResponse is FLAT: {pipeline_running, surveillance_active, error} (surveillance.proto:101-109). The impl passes the body through with no reshape (SurveillanceServiceImpl.java:56-59), so success and status are unknown keys (dropped) and pipeline_running/surveillance_active are never emitted -> client gets an empty message.

FILES:
- Handler: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/SurveillanceApiHandler.java sendSurveillanceStatus (~:342-350) -> CameraDaemon.getSurveillanceStatus().
- Impl: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/SurveillanceServiceImpl.java handleGetStatus :56-59.
- Proto: proto/bladewatch/v1/surveillance.proto:101-109.

FIX: in SurveillanceServiceImpl.handleGetStatus, reshape the REST JSON to the flat proto: map status.initialized (or appropriate field) -> pipeline_running, status.active -> surveillance_active. Confirm the intended semantic mapping (initialized vs enabled vs active) against how the client/UI uses these. If the client needs the richer status fields, consider extending the proto instead (note in the task and flag for human decision).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] GetStatus over Connect returns correct pipeline_running and surveillance_active values.
- [ ] Web UI status still works.
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles.

Do not make mistakes. Read sendSurveillanceStatus, getSurveillanceStatus, SurveillanceServiceImpl, and the proto fully before editing. Verify build + acceptance before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.

title: Vehicle GetGpsLocation/StartGps: 'location' key not reshaped to 'locationJson' (GPS lost)
description:
Epic: BladeWatch-86a. HIGH IMPACT (GPS location entirely lost over Connect).

PROBLEM: GpsApiHandler emits response.put("location", gps.getLocationJson()) (GpsApiHandler.java:51 for GetGpsLocation, :67 for StartGps). The proto field is location_json (json_name locationJson, a string). Key 'location' does not match 'locationJson' -> the client drops it. The impl does no reshaping (unlike System.GetPerformance / Notifications.GetCategories which DO wrap into *_json blobs). success and googleMapsUrl survive.

FILES:
- Handler: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/GpsApiHandler.java :50-52, :65-67.
- Impl: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/VehicleServiceImpl.java (GetGpsLocation/StartGps handlers).
- Proto: proto/bladewatch/v1/vehicle.proto (GetGpsLocationResponse/StartGpsResponse location_json field).
REFERENCE pattern: SystemServiceImpl.handleGetPerformance wraps into performanceJson.

FIX: in VehicleServiceImpl, reshape the captured REST JSON so the 'location' value is moved to key 'locationJson' as a JSON string blob, matching the proto. Confirm getLocationJson() returns a JSON string vs object and stringify accordingly. Do not break the web UI (it reads 'location').

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] GetGpsLocation over Connect returns a non-empty locationJson the client can parse.
- [ ] StartGps likewise.
- [ ] Web UI GPS still works (reads 'location').
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles.

Do not make mistakes. Read GpsApiHandler, VehicleServiceImpl, and the proto fully before editing. Verify build + acceptance before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.

title: Surveillance SetConfig: nested {config:{...}} wrapper makes save a complete no-op
description:
Epic: BladeWatch-86a. HIGH IMPACT (surveillance settings screen save does nothing over Connect).

PROBLEM: The Connect client wraps the payload as SetSurveillanceConfigRequest.config -> wire body {"config":{...}}. But SurveillanceApiHandler.handleConfigPost parses new JSONObject(body) FLAT (~:356) and reads top-level keys (sensitivity, detectPerson, etc.). Because the real values are nested under config, every configJson.has(...) check is false and nothing is saved. Compounding: boolean toggles set to false are default-omitted by the client, so has()-based detection can never turn them OFF even if unwrapped.

FILES:
- Handler: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/SurveillanceApiHandler.java handleConfigPost ~:356+.
- Impl: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/SurveillanceServiceImpl.java handleSetConfig ~:51-54.
- Client: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsClient.kt saveConfig ~:105-128.
- Proto: proto/bladewatch/v1/surveillance.proto SetSurveillanceConfigRequest / SurveillanceConfig.

FIX: in SurveillanceServiceImpl.handleSetConfig, unwrap the nested config object and forward a FLAT body to the REST handler (matching what the web UI sends). Additionally address boolean false toggles: rely on presence flags or send all toggles explicitly. Coordinate with the epic's default-scalar approach. Do NOT break the web UI flat-body POST.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] Changing a surveillance setting in the app and saving persists over Connect (verify via GET config readback).
- [ ] Turning a boolean toggle OFF persists as false.
- [ ] Web UI surveillance config save still works.
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles.

Do not make mistakes. Read handleConfigPost, SurveillanceServiceImpl, and SurveillanceSettingsClient fully before editing. Verify build + acceptance before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.

title: Vehicle MoveWindow: windowIndex/direction ignored ('all open' closes windows)
description:
Epic: BladeWatch-86a. SAFETY-RELEVANT (windows move the wrong way).

PROBLEM: The Connect client sends MoveWindowRequest.window_index (json windowIndex) and direction. The REST handler handleWindow() reads area (~:490) and command (~:511) instead -> window index always resolves to 0 and the open/close direction is ignored (defaults to close). Result: per-window positioning targets the wrong window, and 'all windows open' actually CLOSES them. The targetPercent key is the only one that matches.

FILE: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/VehicleControlApiHandler.java handleWindow() ~:480-525.
PROTO: proto/bladewatch/v1/vehicle.proto MoveWindowRequest (window_index, direction, target_percent, ...). Verify exact field names against the proto before coding.
CLIENT: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleClient.kt windowSetPercent/windowsAllOpen/windowsAllClose/windowsAllVent (~:207-235).

FIX: handleWindow should read windowIndex/direction (proto canonical) with fallback to legacy area/command. Confirm the direction enum/int mapping matches the proto. Keep web UI working.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] windowsAllOpen() over Connect OPENS the windows (not closes).
- [ ] windowSetPercent(windowIndex=2, ...) targets the correct window.
- [ ] Legacy web UI POST with area/command still works.
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles.

title: Vehicle SetSeat: seatIndex ignored, passenger seat commands hit driver

title: Vehicle SetClimate: request keys ignored (temp/fan/restore params)
description:
Epic: BladeWatch-86a. SAFETY-RELEVANT (controls the physical car's AC).

PROBLEM: The Connect client serializes SetClimateRequest with proto camelCase json-names: setpointC, fanLevel, maxCooling, restoreAcOn, restoreTempC, restoreFanLevel. But the REST handler handleClimate() reads the legacy web-UI keys: temp, fan, enabled, hasRestore, restoreTemp, restoreFan, restorePowerOn. None of the climate value keys match, so temperature always defaults to 22C, fan to 3, and ALL max-cooling restore params fall back to defaults -> disabling max cooling restores the wrong AC state.

FILE: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/VehicleControlApiHandler.java
- handleClimate(): lines ~555-584. Reads: req.optDouble("temp",22) (:559,:568), req.optInt("fan",3) (:573), req.optBoolean("enabled",true) (:578), req.optBoolean("hasRestore",true) (:579), req.optDouble("restoreTemp",22) (:580), req.optInt("restoreFan",3) (:581), req.optBoolean("restorePowerOn",true) (:582).
PROTO: proto/bladewatch/v1/vehicle.proto SetClimateRequest (fields: action, on, setpoint_c, fan_level, wind_mode, max_cooling, restore_ac_on, restore_temp_c, restore_fan_level).
CLIENT: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleClient.kt climateOn/climateSetTemp/climateSetFan/climateMaxCooling (~:117-156).

ROOT CAUSE: request-side key drift (see epic). Note the RESPONSE side already emits setpointC/fanLevel correctly (VehicleControlApiHandler.java:313,321) -- only the request reads are wrong.

FIX (pick one, be consistent with the chosen project-wide approach in the epic):
Option A (preferred, web-UI-safe): make handleClimate read BOTH the new proto camelCase keys and fall back to the legacy keys, so the existing web UI keeps working. e.g. read setpointC then temp; fanLevel then fan; maxCooling then enabled; restoreAcOn then restorePowerOn; restoreTempC then restoreTemp; restoreFanLevel then restoreFan.
Option B: reshape the request JSON in VehicleServiceImpl before forwarding to the handler.
CONSTRAINT: Do NOT break the existing web UI which still POSTs the legacy keys to /api/vehicle/climate. Verify the legacy keys still work after the change.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] A SetClimate Connect call with setpointC=24, fanLevel=5 results in handleClimate using 24C and fan 5 (not defaults).
- [ ] climateMaxCooling(enable=true, restoreAcOn=false, restoreTempC=18, restoreFanLevel=2) reaches the handler with those values.
- [ ] Existing web UI POST with temp/fan/restoreTemp still works (legacy fallback).
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew assembleDebug.

Do not make mistakes. Read VehicleControlApiHandler.handleClimate and VehicleClient fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: gRPC/Connect <-> REST 1:1 parity remediation
description:
Umbrella epic tracking parity gaps found in a full review of the Connect/gRPC migration (commit 54653bb).

CONTEXT: The Connect dispatcher passes the request body verbatim to each service impl and writes the impl's JSON response verbatim to the wire (ConnectDispatcher.java:103-106) -- there is NO server-side proto re-encoding. Parity is enforced entirely by the client's JsonFormat: responses parsed with ignoringUnknownFields() (unknown keys dropped to defaults), requests serialized with JsonFormat.printer() (camelCase json-names, default scalars false/0/'' OMITTED).

The parity commit fixed RESPONSE json_name shapes but did NOT fix: (1) REQUEST-side key drift -- handlers still read legacy web-UI keys (temp, fan, position, area, command, view_mode, id) while the Connect client now sends proto camelCase (setpointC, fanLevel, seatIndex, viewMode, tripId); (2) handlers using json.has(key) for booleans cannot receive false/0 because the client omits default scalars; (3) several response shapes still mismatch and drop data.

Child tasks break the findings into individual fixable units. Highest priority: vehicle-control request bugs (wrong temp/seat/window sent to the physical car) and fully-empty responses (GPS, surveillance status).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] All child tasks closed
- [ ] A per-RPC REST-JSON <-> proto contract test exists and passes (its own child task)

Do not make mistakes. This is a tracking epic only; implementation happens in child tasks.
close_reason: All 22 child parity tasks completed and closed; per-RPC wire-parity contract test added (ConnectWireParityTest, 23 tests passing). assembleDebug + full test suite green.

title: Fix: reconcile() and ensureIndexedOnce() can run reconcileInternal() concurrently
description:
## Problem
reconcile() (MediaCatalogManager.java line 138) guards concurrent calls via reconcileInProgress AtomicBoolean but does NOT hold synchronized(this). ensureIndexedOnce() (line 117) holds synchronized(this) for its entire execution including the reconcileInternal() call. The AtomicBoolean guards two concurrent reconcile() calls, but does NOT guard against a concurrent reconcile() + ensureIndexedOnce() pair.

Race window: Thread 1 (HTTP POST /api/recordings/sync) sets reconcileInProgress=true and enters reconcileInternal(). Thread 2 (HTTP GET /api/recordings) enters ensureIndexedOnce(), acquires synchronized(this), and also enters reconcileInternal(). Both independently snapshot scanAllMp4s() and getAllPathState() at different moments. If Thread 1 inserts a row for file X between Thread 2's getAllPathState() call and Thread 2's deletion loop, Thread 2 sees X in dbState but not in its present snapshot and calls database.deleteByPath(X) — deleting the just-inserted row. The freshly indexed recording disappears until the next reconcile.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java

## Fix approach
Option A (simplest): In ensureIndexedOnce(), instead of calling reconcileInternal() directly, call reconcile() — which already has the single-flight CAS guard. If reconcileInProgress is already set (manual sync is running), ensureIndexedOnce() skips the rebuild (or retries after a short delay on a background thread).

Option B: Make reconcileInternal() itself check-and-set reconcileInProgress at its entry, so both callers share the same exclusion regardless of which method they arrive through. ensureIndexedOnce() then just calls reconcileInternal() as before.

Either way, reconcileInProgress must be set BEFORE the scanAllMp4s()/getAllPathState() snapshot is taken.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the AtomicBoolean to a Lock (keep the non-blocking busy result for concurrent callers)
- The autoRebuildAttempted guard in ensureIndexedOnce() must still fire at most once

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Concurrent POST /api/recordings/sync + GET /api/recordings that triggers auto-rebuild cannot both run reconcileInternal() simultaneously (one returns sync_in_progress)
- [ ] reconcileInProgress is set before either snapshot (scanAllMp4s or getAllPathState) is taken
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read MediaCatalogManager.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Changed autoRebuildAttempted to AtomicBoolean; rewrote ensureIndexedOnce() to use CAS and spawn a daemon background thread that calls reconcile() (not reconcileInternal() directly), so reconcileInProgress is always set before any snapshot.

title: Fix: ensureIndexedOnce() blocks HTTP worker thread during full filesystem scan
description:
## Problem
MediaCatalogManager.ensureIndexedOnce() is called directly from RecordingsApiHandler.gatherRecordings() (line 752) on the HTTP request-handling thread. It calls reconcileInternal() synchronously while holding synchronized(this). reconcileInternal() calls RecordingsApiHandler.scanAllMp4s() + indexRecording() for every file — each indexRecording() parses the filename, reads the JSON sidecar from disk, and executes a DB upsert. On a BYD head unit with 300+ clips this can take 15–30 seconds, blocking the HTTP worker for the entire duration. The browser fetch() call times out and the recordings page shows an error.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java (ensureIndexedOnce, reconcileInternal)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/RecordingsApiHandler.java (gatherRecordings, ~line 752)

## Fix approach
Run the rebuild on a background thread. In gatherRecordings(), after detecting db.getCount()==0 and calling ensureIndexedOnce():
- If the DB is empty and the auto-rebuild was just triggered (autoRebuildAttempted just flipped), return gatherFromFilesystem() immediately for this request — the rebuild runs in the background
- ensureIndexedOnce() should post reconcileInternal() to a single-thread daemon executor (e.g. Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor with daemon=true) instead of running it synchronously
- Keep the reconcileInProgress AtomicBoolean so that the background rebuild and a concurrent manual POST /api/recordings/sync don't both run simultaneously

## Constraints
- Do NOT block the HTTP response on the rebuild completion
- The gatherFromFilesystem() fallback must continue to work during the background rebuild
- The background thread must be a daemon thread so it does not prevent JVM exit

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] First GET /api/recordings on a fresh DB returns a response in under 500 ms (via filesystem fallback)
- [ ] After the background reconcile completes (check daemon log for 'Media reconcile: +N'), GET /api/recordings returns DB-sourced results
- [ ] POST /api/recordings/sync during the background rebuild returns {success:false, error:'sync_in_progress'}
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Already fixed by BladeWatch-4h9/kw7: ensureIndexedOnce() now spawns a daemon background thread calling reconcile() and returns immediately. gatherRecordings() falls through to filesystem fallback when count==0, so first HTTP response is fast.

title: Fix: pre-existing recordings permanently invisible when DB has any rows
description:
## Problem
RecordingsApiHandler.gatherRecordings() (line 752) calls ensureIndexedOnce() only when db.getCount()==0. Once even a single row exists (e.g. one newly-recorded clip was live-indexed), any files that pre-date the DB are never surfaced to the UI. There is no startup reconcile, no first-run migration, and no periodic probe to catch the partial-DB case.

## Root cause
MediaCatalogManager.ensureIndexedOnce() guard at line 122: 'if (isAvailable() && database.getCount() == 0)'. This check is correct for a truly empty DB but is wrong when the DB was recently created and some (but not all) files have been indexed. On a device upgrading to this build, the first new recording gets live-indexed, db.getCount() becomes 1, and every subsequent request skips ensureIndexedOnce() forever.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java (or MediaCatalogManager.init())

## Fix approach
After MediaCatalogManager.init() completes successfully, compare db.getCount() with the number of .mp4 files visible to scanAllMp4s() (RecordingsApiHandler.scanAllMp4s()). If the DB has fewer rows than files on disk, schedule one background reconcile (new Thread / daemon executor) so it runs without blocking startup. Do NOT run it on the HTTP worker thread. CameraDaemon already has a staggered startup executor pattern — piggyback on that.

Alternative simpler fix: remove the count==0 guard entirely and always run ensureIndexedOnce() once (still guarded by autoRebuildAttempted), but run it on a background thread rather than the caller's thread.

## Constraints
- Do NOT run the startup reconcile synchronously on the daemon main thread or any HTTP worker
- Do NOT remove the autoRebuildAttempted guard — it must fire at most once per daemon lifetime
- Preserve the filesystem-scan fallback path in gatherRecordings() unchanged

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a fresh daemon start on a device with 50 existing .mp4 files and db.getCount()==0, the recordings list shows all 50 files within a few seconds (after background reconcile completes)
- [ ] After a fresh daemon start on a device with db.getCount()==5 and 50 .mp4 files on disk, the recordings list eventually shows all 50 (background reconcile fires for the missing 45)
- [ ] The HTTP recordings list response is NOT delayed by the reconcile — it returns immediately while the background index builds
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: ensureIndexedOnce() now always schedules a background reconcile regardless of DB count — handles partial-index case. HTTP workers return immediately while reconcile runs in background. count==0 guard removed from gatherRecordings/datesFromDb/aggregateStatsFromDb callers.

title: Fix circular signing cert verification in auto-updater
description:
## Problem
AppUpdater fetches APK updates from github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release. The remote release manifest (bladewatch-update.json) supplies both the APK download URL AND the expected signingCertSha256. The verifyArchiveMetadata() method at AppUpdater.java:741-765 compares the APK's actual signing cert hash against manifest.signingCertSha256. This is circular: whoever controls the GitHub repo controls what cert hash is 'valid', so they can silently install any APK they want.

There is no hardcoded expected certificate SHA256 in the source code — the verification trusts the remote manifest entirely.

## Files
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/updater/AppUpdater.java
  - Line 47: GITHUB_REPO = "yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release"
  - Line 765: return manifest.signingCertSha256.equalsIgnoreCase(certSha256) — the unsafe comparison

## Steps to Fix
1. Read AppUpdater.java fully before changing anything.
2. Determine the correct signing certificate SHA256 for the BladeWatch release keystore (run: keytool -printcert -jarfile <signed.apk> and compute SHA256 of the DER cert bytes, or use: apksigner verify --print-certs app.apk | grep SHA-256).
3. Add a private static final String EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant in AppUpdater.java with the hardcoded cert hash.
4. In verifyArchiveMetadata(), change the final comparison to:
   return EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256.equalsIgnoreCase(certSha256);
   (Do NOT compare against manifest.signingCertSha256 — that's attacker-controlled.)
5. The manifest.signingCertSha256 field can remain as informational/logging only.
6. Build and test that a legitimate release APK still passes verification.
7. Confirm that an APK signed with a different key fails verification.

## Constraints
- Do NOT remove the hash/size checks — keep those as defense-in-depth.
- Do NOT change the GitHub repo URL or update flow mechanics.
- Keep the HTTPS-only URL validation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AppUpdater.java contains a hardcoded EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant
- [ ] verifyArchiveMetadata() compares against the hardcoded constant, not manifest.signingCertSha256
- [ ] ./gradlew test passes
- [ ] Code compiles without errors

Do not make mistakes. Read AppUpdater.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If the correct cert SHA256 value is not determinable from source alone, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: AppUpdater hardcodes expected cert hash; verifyArchiveMetadata compares against it not the manifest; tests pass
close_reason: Structural fix applied: comparison now uses hardcoded EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant instead of manifest. Constant is empty placeholder — must be populated once the release keystore is created (see TODO comment).

title: Fix SentryDaemon LocationStarterActivity Permission Denial from shell UID
description:
## Problem
`LocationStarterActivity` is `android:exported="false"` but SentryDaemon (shell UID 2000) calls `am start` on it from `SentryDaemon.restartLocationService()` Method 1. The system denies cross-UID launch:
```
W/ActivityTaskManager: Permission Denial: starting Intent { act=net.bladewatch.app.START_LOCATION_SILENT cmp=net.bladewatch.app/.ui.LocationStarterActivity } from uid 2000 not exported
```
This means the preferred location restart path fails silently. Method 2 (`am start-foreground-service` on `LocationSidecarService`) IS exported and works, but its result was never logged (now fixed in this session).

## Options
- **Option A** (Recommended): Remove Method 1 entirely since Method 2 already works reliably against the exported `LocationSidecarService`
- **Option B**: Set `android:exported="true"` on `LocationStarterActivity` with an `android:permission="signatureOrSystem"` guard
- **Option C**: Change SentryDaemon to start LocationSidecarService via direct service call instead of through the activity

## Acceptance
- [ ] SentryDaemon successfully restarts location service after it dies
- [ ] No Permission Denial log entries for LocationStarterActivity
- [ ] GPS data continues flowing through LocationSidecarService to daemon IPC port after restart
acceptance_criteria: Verify SentryDaemon can restart location sidecar without Permission Denial
close_reason: Fix implemented: PID-based kill enumeration replaces pkill/killall; LocationStarterActivity method removed

title: Fix Android app auth loop — uid=10117 rejected by TCP IPC on every startup
description:
## Problem
The Android app process (PID 22416, uid=10117) is hammering the TCP IPC server (~once per second) and being rejected every time:

  AUTH: WARN: cannot persist auth secret (likely app UID before daemon boot) — will defer to daemon
  WARN: TCP IPC rejected untrusted peer uid=10117 from 127.0.0.1:xxxxx
  SurveillanceIPC: Surveillance IPC rejected untrusted peer uid=10117

This is a continuous loop — hundreds of rejections per minute. The app keeps retrying but never successfully bootstraps the IPC token.

## Root Cause to Find
- Check AuthManager.java (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/auth/AuthManager.java) and AuthMiddleware.java (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddleware.java) for how uid=10117 is (or is not) permitted.
- Check /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token permissions on device — must be world-readable (mode 644). If it is 600 (shell-only), the app cannot read the bootstrap token and every IPC call will fail.
- Check SecretConfigStore.kt (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/SecretConfigStore.kt) for the defer-to-daemon path — is it retrying immediately with no backoff?
- Check DaemonStartupManager.kt for the retry loop and whether exponential backoff or a max-attempts guard is in place.

## Quick Diagnostic
  adb -s 192.168.0.251:5555 shell ls -la /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token
Expected: -rw-r--r-- (644). If it shows -rw------- (600) that is the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] IPC token file permissions confirmed or corrected to 644
- [ ] Auth retry loop has bounded backoff (not a tight spin loop)
- [ ] App successfully authenticates to daemon without repeated rejections in logcat
- [ ] Fix documented in docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md if permissions were the cause

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed three root causes: (1) PeerCredentials.isTrusted() now falls back to trusting app UIDs (>= 10000) via IPC token gate when createAppContext() returns null-safe PermissionBypassContext — this was the primary block; (2) AuthManager.initialize() has 3s backoff to prevent tight retry loop; (3) IpcTokenManager.generate() now logs warning when setReadable(true,false) fails. Docs updated in ipc-auth-and-secrets.md.

title: Investigate duplicate byd_cam_daemon spawning
description:
## Problem
Two byd_cam_daemon processes (PIDs 14517 and 18199) were found running simultaneously. PID 14517 (the original, ~3h old) holds all server ports (8080, 19876, 19877). PID 18199 was re-launched at ~09:37 by DaemonKeepaliveService or DaemonStartupManager, failed to bind ports (retried at 09:42:33, 09:42:38, 09:42:48), yet the process never exited. The camera_daemon.lock file (/data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.lock) was overwritten to contain PID 18199, breaking the canonical lock reference.

## Root Cause to Find
- What triggered the re-spawn of 18199? Check DaemonKeepaliveService health-check logic and DaemonStartupManager in:
  - app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/DaemonStartupManager.kt
  - app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/AdbDaemonLauncher.kt
  - app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/DaemonBootstrap.java (singleton lock logic)
- Why did the lock file get overwritten by the new instance instead of bailing out on lock contention?
- Why did the second instance not exit after failing MAX_RETRIES port binds?
- Does the start_cam_daemon.sh script check the lock before spawning app_process?

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified (which component triggered the re-spawn)
- [ ] Lock file race condition explained or confirmed not a race
- [ ] Fix proposed or implemented so a second daemon instance exits cleanly when ports are already bound
- [ ] start_cam_daemon.sh verified to check the lock before re-spawning
- [ ] No duplicate daemon processes after fix

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Implemented three-layer fix: (1) CameraDaemon.main() now has a secondary port-availability check before trusting the lock file — connects to TCP:19876, HTTP:8080, and IPC:19877; if any port accepts a connection, exits immediately. This catches cases where FileChannel.tryLock() on tmpfs spuriously allows duplicate lock acquisition. (2) DaemonStartupManager health check now uses the full launch flow (isDaemonRunning + isCameraDaemonResponsive) for camera daemon instead of just ps-based process check, preventing false-positive relaunches from ADB blips. (3) start_cam_daemon.sh watchdog script now checks /proc/<lock-pid> before spawning app_process — if a live PID holds the lock, the watchdog exits.

title: [P1] Log exceptions in critical daemon files (CameraDaemon, AccSentryDaemon, SentryDaemon)
description:
## Context
Part of BladeWatch-jcnf (log all exceptions epic). The three central daemon processes have the most silent exception swallowing. These daemons run as shell-UID app_process outside the Activity lifecycle and are the hardest to debug when they fail silently.

## Files to Fix (21 + 17 + 10 = 48 silent catches)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java (21 silent catches)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/AccSentryDaemon.java (17 silent catches)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/SentryDaemon.java (10 silent catches)

## Logging Pattern to Use
These files use DaemonLogger. Use:
  logger.error("[context] failed: " + e.getMessage(), e);
or if only a static reference is available:
  DaemonLogger.logError(TAG, "[context] failed", e);

## Important Known Patterns
- Shutdown sequences in CameraDaemon (lines ~909-912): multiple monitor .stop() calls in catch(Exception ignored) {} — these SHOULD log at warn/debug level since a failed stop is recoverable but worth knowing about
- Thread.sleep(N) with InterruptedException ignored — add Thread.currentThread().interrupt() after logging, as per Java best practices
- AvmByteCallbackProbe.java is documented as intentional failure isolation — leave those alone unless you are certain they should log

## Step-by-Step Instructions
1. Open each file and search for all catch blocks
2. For each catch (Exception ignored) or catch (Exception e) with no log: add logger.error("...", e)
3. For InterruptedException specifically: also call Thread.currentThread().interrupt()
4. For cleanup/shutdown blocks (resource.close(), monitor.stop()): log at debug or warn level
5. Rebuild: ./gradlew assembleDebug — must compile clean

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CameraDaemon.java has no silent exception catches (except documented intentional ones)
- [ ] AccSentryDaemon.java has no silent exception catches
- [ ] SentryDaemon.java has no silent exception catches
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles without errors
- [ ] ./gradlew test passes

Do not make mistakes. Read each file fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: CameraDaemon, AccSentryDaemon, SentryDaemon have no unlogged catch blocks; build compiles
close_reason: Added exception logging to all silent catch blocks in CameraDaemon.java, AccSentryDaemon.java, and SentryDaemon.java. Used logger.warn/log for cleanup/shutdown catches, added Thread.currentThread().interrupt() for all InterruptedException catches. Build compiles clean.

title: Config: both tripAnalytics and telemetryOverlay are disabled — user action required
description:

  'telemetryOverlay': { 'enabled': false }

- TripConfig.java line 43 also uses false as the default — so any fresh install or cleared config will also have trips disabled (see BladeWatch-ih4z)

This does NOT fix the underlying code bugs. The code bugs (BladeWatch-f920, BladeWatch-ih4z, BladeWatch-l4z2) must also be fixed to ensure features work reliably going forward.

- [ ] bladewatch_config.json shows tripAnalytics.enabled=true after enabling in settings

This is a settings action, not a code change.

title: Bug: StatusOverlay shows daemon unreachable after reboot/reinstall (stale JWT secret)
description:
## Problem
After a fresh install or daemon restart, StatusOverlayService polls show 'daemon unreachable for N polls' even though the daemon IS running. Live logs show pollFails=122+ while CameraDaemon logs show it is actively responding to GetStatus requests. The StatusOverlay shows isRec=false, tripEnabled=false despite the daemon reporting isRecording=true.

## Root Cause
ConnectClientProvider.fetchStatusSync() (ConnectClientProvider.kt:147-150) uses AuthManager.generateJwt() via the jwtInterceptor to authenticate. But after a daemon restart or app reinstall, the device secret cached in the app (from UnifiedConfigManager / bladewatch_config.json) can be stale — it no longer matches the canonical secret the daemon uses to validate JWTs. The daemon returns a non-200 response (401/403), which causes ResponseMessage.Failure, and fetchStatusSync() returns null.

In StatusOverlayService.java:459, fetchStatus() has catch (Exception ignored) which swallows ALL errors. No logging occurs when auth fails — the failure is invisible.

AuthManager.java:283 comment explicitly documents this: 'a daemon restart that hands out the canonical secret won't change config.json's mtime and the app keeps signing JWTs with a stale secret (Invalid signature → Camera unavailable), which previously only cleared after a manual app restart.'

The fix is AuthManager.refresh() — but nothing calls it in the ConnectClientProvider flow.

## Evidence
- Device logcat: StatusOverlay pollFails=122+ with mode=NONE isRec=false
- CameraDaemon logcat: HTTP: POST /bladewatch.v1.SystemService/GetStatus HTTP/1.1 + Battery updated (daemon responding)
- Direct curl with raw IPC token: returns 200 + isRecording=true
- Direct curl without auth: returns {code:invalid_argument}

## Fix Required

### Option A (preferred): Call AuthManager.refresh() when fetchStatusSync returns null N times
In ConnectClientProvider.fetchStatusSync() (ConnectClientProvider.kt:147), if the response is NOT Success, call AuthManager.refresh() to clear the JWT cache, then retry once.

Change:
  @JvmStatic fun fetchStatusSync(): GetStatusResponse? = runBlocking {
      val resp = systemSvc.getStatus(GetStatusRequest.getDefaultInstance(), emptyMap())
      if (resp is ResponseMessage.Success) resp.message else null
  }

To something like:
  @JvmStatic fun fetchStatusSync(): GetStatusResponse? = runBlocking {
      val resp = systemSvc.getStatus(GetStatusRequest.getDefaultInstance(), emptyMap())
      if (resp is ResponseMessage.Success) {
          resp.message
      } else {
          // Auth may be stale after daemon restart — invalidate and retry once
          AuthManager.refresh()
          invalidate()
          val retry = systemSvc.getStatus(GetStatusRequest.getDefaultInstance(), emptyMap())
          if (retry is ResponseMessage.Success) retry.message else null
      }
  }

### Option B: Log the failure
At minimum, in StatusOverlayService.java fetchStatus(), change catch (Exception ignored) to log the exception so failures are visible.

## Files
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/client/ConnectClientProvider.kt:147-150
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/overlay/StatusOverlayService.java:457-463
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/auth/AuthManager.java:277-300 (refresh() docs)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After a fresh daemon start, StatusOverlay successfully reads daemon status within 1-2 poll cycles
- [ ] isRecording, gear, tripEnabled fields reflect actual daemon state
- [ ] Auth errors are logged (not silently swallowed)
- [ ] Build compiles without errors (./gradlew assembleDebug passes)

Do not make mistakes. Read ConnectClientProvider.kt and AuthManager.java fully before editing. Do not change any other auth flows — only the fetchStatusSync retry path. Verify ./gradlew assembleDebug passes before closing.

title: Fix: trip analytics defaults to disabled — no trips recorded on fresh install
description:
## Problem
Trip data does not show up in the UI after a drive. One root cause: TripConfig.enabled defaults to false, so on a fresh install (or any device where the config file has no 'tripAnalytics' section), trips are never initialized.

## Root Cause
TripConfig.java line 21 and 31: private boolean enabled = false; / this.enabled = false;
TripConfig.java line 43: enabled = section.optBoolean('enabled', false); (default false even if section exists)
TripAnalyticsManager.java line 67: if (config.isEnabled()) { initComponents(); } — gates ALL trip initialization behind enabled flag

If /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_config.json has no 'tripAnalytics' section (fresh device), load() returns false, enabled stays false, TripDetector/TripDatabase/TripTelemetryRecorder are never created, and no trips are ever detected or recorded.

## Fix Required
File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/trips/TripConfig.java

Change line 43 default from false to true:
  enabled = section.optBoolean('enabled', false);
→ enabled = section.optBoolean('enabled', true);

Also change constructor default (line 31):
  this.enabled = false;
→ this.enabled = true;

And field initializer (line 21):
  private boolean enabled = false;
→ private boolean enabled = true;

This makes trips opt-out (default on) rather than opt-in (default off). The UI toggle in trips.js can still disable it explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On a device with no prior config file, TripAnalyticsManager.init() calls initComponents()
- [ ] After a drive, trip appears in the UI
- [ ] Setting enabled=false in config still disables trips
- [ ] Build compiles without errors (./gradlew assembleDebug passes)

Do not make mistakes. Read TripConfig.java fully before editing. Verify ./gradlew assembleDebug passes before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix: telemetry overlay not burned into auto-start dashcam recordings
description:
## Problem
After a real drive, dashcam recordings have no telemetry overlay (speed, GPS, gear, etc.) burned into the video.

## Root Cause
GpuSurveillancePipeline.java line 1061 incorrectly gates telemetry polling start behind recorder.isOverlayEnabled():

  if (telemetryCollector != null && recorder.isOverlayEnabled()) {
      telemetryCollector.setOverlayRecordingActive(true);
      telemetryCollector.startPolling();
  }

The overlay feature defaults to disabled in config (CameraDaemon.java:1350: optBoolean('enabled', false)). So recorder.isOverlayEnabled() returns false, telemetryCollector.startPolling() is never called, and OverlayBitmapRenderer gets null/stale snapshots — producing blank overlay frames that are then composited (or not) into the video.

Compare: explicit startRecording() calls at GpuSurveillancePipeline.java:1232+ have NO isOverlayEnabled() check and always start polling. Auto-start path (line 1056) is the inconsistent one.

## Fix Required
File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/GpuSurveillancePipeline.java
Line: 1061

Change:
  if (telemetryCollector != null && recorder.isOverlayEnabled()) {

To:
  if (telemetryCollector != null) {

This makes the auto-start path consistent with the explicit startRecording() path at lines 1232-1235, 1284-1286.

## Overlay pipeline for context
1. TelemetryDataCollector (must call startPolling() to collect data)
2. OverlayBitmapRenderer.java:139-254 (renders speed/GPS/gear to 1280x80 bitmap)
3. OverlayDoubleBuffer.java (thread-safe double buffer)
4. GpuMosaicRecorder.java:413-476 (GPU composites overlay onto video)
5. GpuSurveillancePipeline.java (recording lifecycle controller)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After a drive, recordings have telemetry data burned into the overlay region
- [ ] isOverlayEnabled() only controls whether the overlay is rendered to video, NOT whether telemetry is collected
- [ ] Build compiles without errors (./gradlew assembleDebug passes)
- [ ] No regression to explicit startRecording() paths

Do not make mistakes. Read GpuSurveillancePipeline.java fully (especially lines 1050-1070 and 1225-1290) before editing. Do not change anything other than the one condition on line 1061. Verify ./gradlew assembleDebug passes before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit runBlocking Connect calls off the main thread (NetworkOnMainThread/ANR risk)
description:
## Problem
Every Connect client method wraps the suspend RPC in kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking { }. If any of these is called from the Android main/UI thread, Android throws NetworkOnMainThreadException (hard crash) or blocks the UI for up to the OkHttp read timeout (10s standard, 120s long). This regression risk appears with the gRPC migration; verify all call sites run on a background dispatcher.

## Files to audit
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleClient.kt + VehicleController.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/trips/TripsClient.kt + TripsController.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/recording/RecordingSettingsClient.kt + RecordingSettingsController.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsClient.kt + SurveillanceSettingsController.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/liveview/LiveStreamClient.kt + LiveViewController.kt

## Steps
1. For each *Client.kt method, trace the controller/fragment call site and confirm it executes on Dispatchers.IO / a background thread / executor, NOT the main thread.
2. For any main-thread call site, move the call to a coroutine on Dispatchers.IO (or the existing background executor) and post results back to the UI.
3. Prefer converting the runBlocking-based clients to suspend functions invoked from a lifecycleScope/viewModelScope on IO, OR keep runBlocking but guarantee it is only ever invoked off-main.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No Connect RPC (runBlocking) executes on the Android main thread (verified by code trace + a StrictMode or manual on-device check with no NetworkOnMainThreadException).
- [ ] UI does not freeze when the daemon is slow/unreachable (long-timeout calls do not block main thread).
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlin passes.

Do not make mistakes. Read each client and its controller fully before editing. Do not change RPC semantics. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Audited all 63 call sites of the 5 runBlocking gRPC clients (Vehicle/Trips/RecordingSettings/SurveillanceSettings/LiveStream): every call is wrapped in a Thread/Executor (or, for LiveStreamClient, entered on main then internally spawns its decoder thread) — NONE run on the main thread. Android also enforces NetworkOnMainThreadException by default, so a regression cannot fail silently. Added a debug-only StrictMode.ThreadPolicy().detectNetwork().penaltyLog() guard in BladeWatchApplication.onCreate (BuildConfig.DEBUG) as a forward regression detector. compileDebugKotlin BUILD SUCCESSFUL. No main-thread bug existed; no RPC semantics changed.

title: Add HTTP round-trip test for Connect unary content-type negotiation
description:
## Problem
ConnectWireParityTest only validates JSON serialization shape; it never exercises the actual HTTP transport, so it missed the 415 content-type outage that took down the entire gRPC UI. Add a test that drives a real (or in-process) Connect HTTP request through ConnectDispatcher/HttpServer and asserts the content-type negotiation.

## Files
- app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ (new test, e.g. ConnectContentTypeNegotiationTest.java)
- Reference: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java
- Reference: app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectWireParityTest.java (existing patterns)

## Steps
1. Construct a request to ConnectDispatcher.dispatch() (or through HttpServer) for a representative unary RPC with Content-Type: application/json and Connect-Protocol-Version: 1.
2. Assert the response status is NOT 415 and the response Content-Type is application/json.
3. Add a negative case: Content-Type: text/html -> 415.
4. Add a streaming-form case: application/connect+json accepted, response application/connect+json.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Test fails against the pre-fix dispatcher (415) and passes after the content-type fixes.
- [ ] ./gradlew test --tests "*ConnectContentTypeNegotiation*" passes.
- [ ] Test does not require a physical device (in-process or localhost socket).

Do not make mistakes. Read the existing connect tests before writing. Verify the test actually drives the dispatcher (not just serialization). If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added app/src/test/.../ConnectContentTypeNegotiationTest.java: 10 tests covering helper negotiation + in-process dispatch() round-trip (unary json accepted+echoed, streaming echoed, charset/case tolerance, unsupported/null rejected). Fails against pre-fix dispatcher, passes now. testDebugUnitTest BUILD SUCCESSFUL, tests=10 failures=0.

title: TripsClient.fetchRange reads non-existent keys (estimatedKm/soc always 0.0)
description:
Epic: BladeWatch-86a. CLIENT-SIDE bug (in-scope, fix in Kotlin).

PROBLEM: TripsClient.fetchRange reads range.optDouble("estimatedKm") and range.optDouble("soc") from the rangeJson blob (TripsClient.kt:143-145). But the daemon's RangeEstimate.toJson() (RangeEstimate.java:25-30) emits predictedRangeKm, lowerBoundKm, upperBoundKm, bucketKey, sampleCount, builtInRangeKm -- there is no estimatedKm and no soc. So estimatedKm and soc are always 0.0; only builtInKm (reads builtInRangeKm) is correct.

title: Epic: REST<->gRPC (Connect) response parity — Connect responses silently drop fields
description:
## Epic: REST <-> gRPC (Connect) response parity

### Background
The daemon's Connect/gRPC endpoints do NOT serialize from proto. Each Connect impl in
app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/*ServiceImpl.java shells the
matching REST handler and returns its hand-written JSON body VERBATIM
(see ConnectHandlerUtil.captureString, app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java:161).

The native Android client (ConnectClientProvider.kt) parses that JSON into generated proto
messages using connect-kotlin 0.6.0 GoogleJavaJSONStrategy, which uses
JsonFormat.parser().ignoringUnknownFields() (confirmed by decompile). Therefore any REST JSON
key that does NOT equal the proto field's canonical JSON name is SILENTLY DROPPED, leaving that
proto field at its default (0 / false / ""). No exception is thrown. This produces wrong UI such
as "SD unavailable" (sd_card_free_bytes parses as 0).

### Fix direction (applies to all child tasks)
- The web UI reads the REST keys directly (e.g. surveillance.js reads data.cameraFps, cdrUsage).
  Do NOT rename REST handler keys — that breaks the web UI.
- The Kotlin client reads the generated proto accessors (e.g. m.sdCardTotalBytes,
  m.recordingsSizeBytes). Do NOT rename proto fields — that changes accessor names the Kotlin code
  depends on.
- The correct, non-breaking fix for a pure NAME mismatch is to add [json_name = "<exact REST key>"]
  to the proto field so the proto's wire JSON name equals the key the daemon already emits.
- After editing any .proto, regenerate the committed stubs with: ./gradlew generateConnectProtos
  (requires the `buf` CLI). This rewrites generated Java/Kotlin under
  app/src/main/java/net/bladewatch/app/grpc/v1/ and TS under web/src/gen. The committed stubs MUST
  be regenerated, not hand-edited (json_name is embedded in the descriptor bytes). Then verify
  ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes.

### Children
This epic tracks all parity fixes. It is blocked by its child tasks and should be closed only when
all children are closed and a full audit of every Connect response message confirms 1:1 parity.

This is a tracking epic — no code changes here.
close_reason: All child parity tasks complete. json_name name-mismatch fixes (Storage, Settings, Vehicle, SafeLocations, RecordingEntry); structural fixes via Connect-impl reshape (Trips telemetry/summary/range/detail/gps, Recordings GetStats nested + EventTimeline blob + detected_classes); proto aligned to emitted shape (Surveillance heatmap grid + filterlog strings); wrappers (Performance, Categories); unused fields removed (gps_json, battery status/is_charging/status_string, ModelInfo.url, ListModelsResponse.success, active_cameras, PreviewCleanupFile.age_hours); plus the two earlier RecordingsService routing fixes. Two residuals surfaced for follow-up: (1) RecordingEntry.duration_seconds is consumed by the Angular recording page but has no emitter data source; (2) handleListRecordings ignores ListRecordingsRequest filters/pagination over Connect. Each task verified with buf regenerate + compileDebugJavaWithJavac (Java + Angular) BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

title: Fix: unauthenticated Connect RPC calls receive HTML redirect instead of 401 JSON
description:
## Problem

AuthMiddleware.handleUnauthorized() (line 223 of AuthMiddleware.java) checks a hardcoded list of path prefixes to decide whether to return a JSON 401 or redirect to login.html:

  if (path.startsWith("/api/") || path.startsWith("/ws") || path.startsWith("/snapshot/") || ...)
      → return JSON 401
  else
      → return HTTP 302 redirect to /login.html?redirect=...

Connect RPC paths follow the pattern /bladewatch.v1.ServiceName/MethodName (e.g. /bladewatch.v1.TripsService/ListTrips). These do NOT match any of the checked prefixes. So when a JWT expires or is absent:
1. The Connect client sends a request to /bladewatch.v1.TripsService/ListTrips
2. Auth fails → handleUnauthorized is called
3. Client receives HTTP 302 with Location: /login.html?redirect=/bladewatch.v1.TripsService/ListTrips
4. OkHttp or the Connect stub receives HTML instead of a Connect error envelope
5. The call fails with a parse error, not a structured 'unauthenticated' ConnectException

The only Connect path that is correctly handled is /bladewatch.v1.AuthService/Login because it is in PUBLIC_PATHS and bypasses auth entirely.

## Fix

Add /bladewatch.v1. to the machine-readable path prefix check in handleUnauthorized():
  if (path.startsWith("/api/") || path.startsWith("/ws") ||
      path.startsWith("/snapshot/") || path.startsWith("/video/") ||
      path.startsWith("/thumb/") || path.startsWith("/h264/") ||
      path.equals("/status") || path.startsWith("/bladewatch.v1."))  // ADD THIS

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddleware.java (line 223)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GET /bladewatch.v1.TripsService/ListTrips with no JWT returns HTTP 401 JSON (not 302)
- [ ] GET /bladewatch.v1.SurveillanceService/GetConfig with no JWT returns HTTP 401 JSON (not 302)
- [ ] Existing /api/* behavior is unchanged (still returns 401 JSON)
- [ ] Existing page requests (/ and unknown pages) still redirect to /login.html
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read AuthMiddleware.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing.

title: Fix: captureString/captureWithCookies silently forward HTTP 4xx/5xx as Connect 200 OK
description:
## Problem

ConnectHandlerUtil.captureRaw() splits HTTP headers from body bytes but stores the HTTP status line (e.g. 'HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found') in headersSection and never parses it. Neither capture(), captureString(), nor captureWithCookies() inspect the HTTP status code.

All service impls except TripsServiceImpl use captureString() or captureWithCookies(). This means:
- When a wrapped REST handler calls HttpResponse.sendError(out, 404, ...) or sendError(out, 400, ...), captureString() returns that error body as a ConnectResponse — and the ConnectDispatcher sends HTTP 200 OK to the client.
- The Connect client has no way to distinguish success from failure except by parsing the body.
- A plain-text error body (not JSON) becomes '{}' (empty JSONObject) after capture() fails to parse it.

Affected service impls: RecordingsServiceImpl, VehicleServiceImpl, SurveillanceServiceImpl, AuthServiceImpl (handleLogout, handleGetAuthStatus), SettingsServiceImpl, SafeLocationsServiceImpl, StorageServiceImpl, StreamServiceImpl, NotificationsServiceImpl, SystemServiceImpl, UpdateServiceImpl.

TripsServiceImpl is the ONLY correct impl — it uses TripApiHandler.handleRequest() which returns _status, and explicitly checks status >= 400 before throwing ConnectException.

## Fix

In ConnectHandlerUtil.captureRaw(), after finding the \r\n\r\n separator, parse the HTTP status code from the first line of headersSection:
  String statusLine = headers.split("\r\n")[0]; // e.g. 'HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found'
  int status = Integer.parseInt(statusLine.split(" ")[1]);
Store status in RawCapture. Then in captureString() and captureWithCookies(), check the status and throw the appropriate ConnectException if status >= 400. Map HTTP status → Connect error code using the same table already in ConnectDispatcher.connectCodeToHttpStatus() (in reverse). 400 → 'invalid_argument', 401 → 'unauthenticated', 403 → 'permission_denied', 404 → 'not_found', 409 → 'already_exists', 429 → 'resource_exhausted', 500/503 → 'internal'.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java (primary)
  - Add int httpStatus to RawCapture
  - Parse status in captureRaw()
  - Add status check in captureString() and captureWithCookies()

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] captureString() throws ConnectException("not_found", ...) when the wrapped handler returns HTTP 404
- [ ] captureString() throws ConnectException("invalid_argument", ...) when the wrapped handler returns HTTP 400
- [ ] captureWithCookies() throws ConnectException("unauthenticated", ...) when the wrapped handler returns HTTP 401
- [ ] captureString() returns ConnectResponse.of(body) when handler returns HTTP 200
- [ ] TripsServiceImpl._status behavior is unchanged (it does not use captureString)
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read ConnectHandlerUtil.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing.

title: VehicleClient.vehicleCommand() ignores body success flag: rejected car commands reported as success
description:
Physical-car commands (Lock/Unlock/Trunk/MoveWindow/SetClimate/etc.) report success in the UI even when the BYD cloud rejects them, because the rewritten Connect helper only checks transport success.

DETAIL: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleClient.kt vehicleCommand() (~line 262-269) returns 'resp is ResponseMessage.Success' (line 265) — it only checks the ConnectRPC transport succeeded and never reads the body-level success field. VehicleCommandResponse declares 'bool success = 1' (proto/bladewatch/v1/vehicle.proto ~line 185-189). The OLD code's postSuccess helper (HEAD~1 VehicleClient.kt ~line 159-161) checked BOTH HTTP 2xx AND resp.optBoolean("success", false). The daemon returns rejected commands as normal HTTP 200 with {"success":false} (VehicleControlApiHandler.java ~line 521/969-970, sent via HttpResponse.sendJson). So a BYD-rejected command (car offline/asleep/denied) now shows as success.

FIX: vehicleCommand() must return true only when resp is Success AND the response message's success field is true. Apply to every command method that uses this helper.

RELATED (verify while here): VehicleClient seat calls (~line 157-188) reportedly dropped the full driver/passenger heat+vent state that the old code commented 'must be sent on every seat call - cloud API is stateful', and climateMaxCooling dropped its restore-point params. VehicleServiceImpl forwards the Connect body unchanged, so missing fields are genuinely gone. Confirm the proto SetSeat/SetClimate requests carry all required stateful fields and the client populates them.

- [ ] UI surfaces an error/retry when a command is rejected by the cloud.

title: ConnectRPC login delivers no session: capture() strips Set-Cookie header
description:
The Connect AuthService Login path never delivers the JWT session cookie to the client, so web login over ConnectRPC is non-functional.

ROOT CAUSE: ConnectHandlerUtil.capture() (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java around line 36-38) adapts existing REST handlers by capturing their full raw HTTP response, splitting on the first blank line (\r\n\r\n), and returning ONLY the body substring. This discards ALL headers, including Set-Cookie. AuthApiHandler delivers the JWT exclusively via a Set-Cookie: byd_session=<jwt> header (AuthApiHandler.handleTokenValidation around line 165-172; cookie written by HttpResponse.sendJsonWithCookies). The JSON body only contains {success, deviceId, expiresIn} — no token. AuthServiceImpl.handleLogin (server/connect/impl/AuthServiceImpl.java line 27-28) routes through captureString, so byd_session is stripped and the browser never stores the session.

FIX DIRECTION: The Connect adapter must propagate Set-Cookie headers from the wrapped REST handler to the Connect HTTP response. Either (a) have capture() return both headers and body and have the dispatcher re-emit Set-Cookie, or (b) special-case AuthService to forward cookies. Note byd_session is HttpOnly (good — keep it); the frontend auth.service.ts/auth.interceptor.ts currently read document.cookie for byd_session which cannot see HttpOnly cookies — coordinate the auth-token delivery design so the browser actually gets an auth credential the interceptor can use.

FILES: server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java, server/connect/impl/AuthServiceImpl.java, server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java, web/src/app/core/auth/auth.service.ts, web/src/app/core/connect/auth.interceptor.ts.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] A Connect AuthService/Login call results in the byd_session cookie being set on the HTTP response (verify Set-Cookie present in the Connect response headers).
- [ ] After login, subsequent ConnectRPC calls are authenticated (auth.interceptor attaches the credential or the HttpOnly cookie is sent automatically same-origin).
- [ ] The auth guard no longer bounces a freshly-logged-in user back to /login.
- [ ] Build compiles (./gradlew assembleDebug) and existing AuthManagerTest/AuthMiddlewareTest pass.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Add per-stage timing instrumentation to GpuSurveillancePipeline (rolling p50/p95)
description:

Today the pipeline logs only CONFIGURED fps/resolution/bitrate (see app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/GpuSurveillancePipeline.java:330 and app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/GpuPipelineFactory.java:129) — never MEASURED stage latency. This is the single biggest optimization gap.

CONSTRAINTS — do NOT change: the pipeline's actual processing logic, frame ordering, threading model, or encoder config. This is observability only. Do not add per-frame log spam. Do not allocate objects per frame.
