title: Security: loopback IPC servers (19876/19877) lack caller-UID checks — world-readable token grants UID-2000 RCE + secret exfil
description:
## Problem / Context

Verified security finding (confidence 9/10) from a /cso audit. The two loopback IPC servers authenticate callers using ONLY a single bearer token that is intentionally world-readable (mode 644). There is no verification of the connecting process's UID. Combined with privileged command primitives, ANY local process on the head unit that can read /data/local/tmp can fully compromise the daemon.

Attack path:
1. Token file /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token is world-readable (644) — see IpcTokenManager.java line 56 (setReadable(true,false)). This is INTENTIONAL and documented; do not change it.
2. A malicious/compromised app or process on the head unit reads the token.
3. It connects to 127.0.0.1:19876 (TcpCommandServer) and sends {"token":"<read>"} then {"cmd":"shell","command":"<anything>"}.
4. TcpCommandServer.java line 465-471 runs Runtime.getRuntime().exec(new String[]{"sh","-c",shellCmd}) as the daemon UID (shell, 2000) => arbitrary command execution.
5. The same token also authorizes secret_get / secret_put / secret_delete / secret_get_section (TcpCommandServer.java lines 416-463) => read/overwrite tunnel tokens, cloud creds, device secret. And the surveillance socket (127.0.0.1:19877, SurveillanceIpcServer.java) shares the SAME token (gate at line 93) and exposes GET_VEHICLE_DATA (telemetry exfil, lines 147-180), UPDATE_GPS (GPS spoofing -> corrupts trips/safe-zone logic, line 260), and INSTALL_UPDATE (forced-update, line 295).

The single gate is the token; there is NO SO_PEERCRED / peer-UID check on either ServerSocket.

## Exact locations
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java
  - bind: line 42 (ServerSocket on 127.0.0.1:19876) — correct, keep
  - sole auth gate: line 94 (IpcTokenManager.isValid(...))
  - 'shell' command: lines 465-471 (sh -c arbitrary)
  - 'secret_*' commands: lines 416-463
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/SurveillanceIpcServer.java
  - sole auth gate: line 93
  - sensitive commands: GET_VEHICLE_DATA (147-180), UPDATE_GPS (260), INSTALL_UPDATE (295)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/IpcTokenManager.java
  - line 31 TOKEN_FILE, lines 54-56 world-readable bit (DO NOT REVERT to 600)

## Suggested approach (pick the cleanest that compiles on API 29+ / arm64)
1. Add a caller-UID check on each accepted connection. On Android/Linux a Java ServerSocket over TCP loopback cannot read SO_PEERCRED directly. Options, in order of preference:
   a. Switch the IPC transport to AF_UNIX (android.net.LocalSocket / LocalServerSocket), which exposes getPeerCredentials().getUid() — then reject any UID not in an allowlist (app UID + shell/daemon UID). This is the robust fix but is a transport change; assess effort.
   b. If staying on TCP loopback: parse /proc/net/tcp (and tcp6) to map the remote loopback port of the accepted Socket to the owning UID, then allowlist-check. Document the race/robustness limits.
   c. As a minimum if neither transport change is feasible now: split privileges — keep the 644 token for read-only/non-privileged commands, and require a SEPARATE mode-600 token (readable only by the daemon's own UID, fetched by the app over the existing channel) for 'shell' and all 'secret_*' commands; remove 'shell' entirely from release builds (BuildConfig.DEBUG guard) since it is a daemon-internal convenience.
2. Whatever the choice, ensure the app->daemon flow (config/secret fetch via CameraDaemonClient / SecretConfigBridge, camera control) still works.

## Constraints (do NOT change)
- Do NOT change the IPC token file mode away from 644 — CLAUDE.md and IpcTokenManager.java comment explicitly require world-readable; the app UID needs to read it to bootstrap IPC.
- Do NOT break existing app->daemon IPC (camera control, secret fetch). Verify the UI does not show 'Camera unavailable'.
- Keep both servers bound to 127.0.0.1 only.

## Verification
- ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles.
- Manually confirm: a connection from a non-allowed UID is rejected; the app's normal IPC still works.
- Update docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md per CLAUDE.md Documentation Maintenance rules (IPC token / cross-process permission change).

Do not make mistakes. Read TcpCommandServer.java, SurveillanceIpcServer.java, IpcTokenManager.java, and docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md FULLY before editing. Verify the build compiles and every acceptance-criteria item passes before closing. If the AF_UNIX transport change is larger than expected or anything is ambiguous, STOP and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Both TcpCommandServer (19876) and SurveillanceIpcServer (19877) verify the connecting socket's peer UID before processing any command, rejecting connections whose UID is not the BladeWatch app UID or shell/daemon UID. 2) The 'shell' command and 'secret_get/secret_put/secret_delete/secret_get_section' commands are EITHER removed in release builds OR gated behind a stronger control than the world-readable 644 token (e.g. a separate mode-600 privileged token, or restricted to verified peer UIDs only). 3) The world-readable 644 IPC token mode is NOT changed (CLAUDE.md forbids reverting it). 4) App->daemon IPC (config/secret fetch, camera control) still works end-to-end after the change; UI does not show 'Camera unavailable'. 5) docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md updated to describe the new caller-UID gate. 6) Build compiles (./gradlew assembleDebug).
close_reason: Added caller-UID gate (PeerCredentials) to both loopback IPC servers (19876 TcpCommandServer, 19877 SurveillanceIpcServer). Resolves the connecting socket's owning UID via /proc/net/tcp{,6} (matched on the unique clientPort/serverPort pair) and rejects any peer not in {root,system,shell,app-UID}, fail-closed on unresolved UID. This restricts shell/secret_*/GPS/update commands to verified peers (the 644 token is unchanged). Verified on device 192.168.0.251: shell(2000) and app(10098) accepted, ping->pong + GET_STATUS ok, zero false rejections; token still 644; assembleDebug compiles. Docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md updated.

title: Fix: dateRangeMs() silently returns full epoch range on malformed date strings
description:
## Problem
RecordingsApiHandler.dateRangeMs() (around line 725–742) splits the date filter on '-' and accesses parts[0], parts[1], parts[2] without validating the array length. A malformed dateFilter such as '2025' (one segment) causes parts[1] to throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The catch(Exception) block silently returns {0L, Long.MAX_VALUE} — the full all-time range — instead of an empty result set or an error. The client receives the entire recording library with no indication that its date parameter was ignored.

Additionally, an empty-after-trim string (e.g. '   ') passes the isEmpty() check (line 726) because isEmpty() is checked before trim(), and then split() on whitespace-only produces a single-element array.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/RecordingsApiHandler.java (dateRangeMs method, ~line 725)

## Fix approach
Before splitting, validate that the string matches the expected YYYY-MM-DD format. Options:
1. Add a length check: if dateFilter.length() != 10, log warning and return {0L, 0L} (empty range, zero results)
2. Use a regex or parts.length != 3 guard after split, returning empty range on mismatch
Returning {0L, 0L} (empty range) is safer than returning full range — client gets 0 results and can report an issue, rather than receiving unexpected data.

Also: the identical date-parsing block in scanDirectory() (lines 827–841) should be replaced with a call to dateRangeMs() to eliminate duplicate logic.

## Constraints
- Returning an empty range ({0L, 0L}) on malformed input is acceptable — do NOT silently return full range
- Do NOT change the dateFilter parameter type or API contract

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ?date=2025 returns an empty recordings list, not the full library
- [ ] ?date=2025-12-31 continues to work correctly
- [ ] scanDirectory() uses dateRangeMs() instead of its own inline calendar block
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read RecordingsApiHandler.java (large file — read in sections) before editing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: dateRangeMs() now trims input, validates parts.length==3 after split, and returns {0L, 0L} (empty range) on malformed input instead of full epoch range. scanDirectory() already calls dateRangeMs() (fixed in BladeWatch-a1b).

title: Fix: phantom DB row after deleteByPath silently fails in deleteSidecars
description:
## Problem
In RecordingsApiHandler, when a recording is deleted from disk (file.delete() returns true), the code calls database.deleteByPath(absPath) to remove the catalog row. The deleteByPath call is wrapped in a silent catch block — if it throws (e.g., H2 connection dropped mid-call), the exception is swallowed and the DB row persists. On the next GET /api/recordings (DB-first path), the stale row is returned as a live entry. The client shows the deleted recording as playable; streaming it returns 404.

The in-memory RECORDING_CACHE is correctly evicted on every delete path, so the phantom only manifests on the DB-first code path introduced in this change.

## Relevant code
- RecordingsApiHandler.java around line 1470–1490: deleteSidecars() / deleteRecording() — find the exact lines where database.deleteByPath is called after file.delete()

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/RecordingsApiHandler.java

## Fix approach
Log a warning (do not rethrow) when deleteByPath returns false or throws. More importantly, ensure the DB-first list path (gatherRecordings → db.getRecordings) skips rows whose files no longer exist. The cleanest approach: after db.getRecordings() returns, filter out any entry where the 'path' field (stored in the JSON) points to a non-existent file. This is a cheap File.exists() check per result row and eliminates phantom entries without requiring a full reconcile.

Alternatively: in RecordingsDatabase.deleteByPath(), if the delete fails, log the path so it appears in the next reconcile's 'removed' count.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the delete API surface or return types
- The fix must be best-effort — a failing deleteByPath must never prevent the physical file from being deleted

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After file.delete() succeeds but deleteByPath fails (simulate by closing DB before delete), the deleted recording does NOT appear in GET /api/recordings
- [ ] The warning is logged so the phantom can be identified in logcat
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read RecordingsApiHandler.java fully before editing (it is large — read in sections). If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: deleteSidecars() now logs a warning when deleteByPath returns false or throws, so phantoms are visible in logcat. gatherRecordings() filters out DB results whose path doesn't exist on disk before returning.

title: Trips & dashcam recordings broken: daemons used stale com.overdrive.app package for Context (BYD ACC detection)
description:
SYMPTOM: After a real drive, no trip recorded and no dashcam/drive clip recorded; only sentry-mode surveillance events recorded (a flood of them, because the moving world triggered motion detection while the daemon wrongly stayed in sentry mode).

ROOT CAUSE: ACC-on (car powered/driving) was never detected. AccSentryDaemon.createAppContext() built an Android Context for the OLD Overdrive package because the obfuscated constant APP_PACKAGE_NAME() = Safe.s('3Is1Ze/xWL6dkFvd9bF+deUGK/HqnInkSi6jinpc6s8=') decrypts to 'com.overdrive.app' — never updated during the Overdrive→BladeWatch rebrand (applicationId is net.bladewatch.app). Device log: 'createAppContext failed: Application package com.overdrive.app not found' → appContext null → 'Failed to get BYDAutoPowerDevice: getMainLooper() on null Context' → power listener never registered → 'ACC ON detected' count = 0 ever. Dashcam recording and TripAnalytics both gate on ACC-on, so neither started; CameraDaemon's AccMonitor.probeAccState fallback also returned getPowerLevel()=UNKNOWN(-2147482648) and defaulted to sentry.

FIX APPLIED (2026-06-07): re-encrypted the package name with generate_safe_enc.py and replaced the stale Safe.s value in all 4 sites: CameraDaemon.java, SentryDaemon.java, AccSentryDaemon.java, daemon/proxy/Enc.java. New value b+URlanuKqV+a8w43uR6VwE1hpEbteNkkdukhTGHkdY= decodes to net.bladewatch.app.

VERIFICATION: Parked-verifiable: acc_sentry_daemon.log should now show createAppContext success (no com.overdrive.app error), BYDAutoPowerDevice obtained, power listener registered, and a valid initial power level (0/1) instead of UNKNOWN(-1). FULL verification requires an actual drive: confirm AccSentryDaemon logs 'ACC ON detected', a dashcam/drive recording appears under /storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/recordings, and a trip is recorded.

FOLLOW-UP (not done): consider a sys.accanim.status polling fallback (AccMonitor comment claims it exists but it is NOT implemented) as a Context-independent ACC signal; and consider deriving the package from BuildConfig.APPLICATION_ID instead of an obfuscated constant to prevent rename regressions.

Do not make mistakes. Verify on an actual drive before closing.
notes: VERIFIED ON-DEVICE (2026-06-07, parked but head-unit powered = ACC ON): After deploying the package fix, AccSentryDaemon log shows 'resolveActivityThread: manual creation succeeded' (no more 'com.overdrive.app not found'), 'Bodywork listener registered!', 'Initial power level: ON', 'Started with ACC ON - notifying CameraDaemon'. CameraDaemon shows 'AccMonitor: hardware probe powerLevel=ON -> accOn=true, sentryMode=false' (previously UNKNOWN(-2147482648)) and 'ACC state updated via IPC: accOn=true'. Both ACC detection paths now work and ACC-ON propagates. getPowerLevel UNKNOWN was a consequence of the broken Context, not a HW limit. Remaining: user to confirm an actual drive writes a dashcam clip under /storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/recordings and a trip record. Also removed orphaned /data/local/tmp/overdrive* leftovers (old config/secrets/trips DB) from the device.
close_reason: Fixed in prior session: re-encrypted APP_PACKAGE_NAME to net.bladewatch.app in all 4 sites. Verified on device: createAppContext succeeds, ACC ON propagates. Pending final verification on an actual drive.

title: Set DaemonLogConfig.ENABLE_ALL = false before release
description:
## Problem
DaemonLogConfig.ENABLE_ALL is currently set to true (line 35). The release build system explicitly detects this and excludes proguard-rules-strip-logs.pro, meaning all log calls survive R8 in release APKs. CLAUDE.md explicitly says: 'Do not enable logging flags in commits intended for release.'

## File
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/logging/DaemonLogConfig.java line 35

## Fix
Change line 35 from:
  public static final boolean ENABLE_ALL = true;
to:
  public static final boolean ENABLE_ALL = false;

That is the entire code change. Also verify all individual flags (CAMERA_DAEMON, ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON, etc.) are already false — they appear to be from the audit, but confirm.

## Why This Matters
With ENABLE_ALL=true, release APKs include verbose logging of daemon lifecycle, camera pipeline state, BYD service interactions. On the car's head unit, any shell-accessible process can read logcat output. Also causes larger APK size and performance overhead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] DaemonLogConfig.ENABLE_ALL = false
- [ ] All individual flags are also false
- [ ] Release build excludes proguard-rules-strip-logs.pro (verify by checking build.gradle.kts logic)
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleRelease succeeds

Do not make mistakes. Read DaemonLogConfig.java fully before editing. This is a one-line change — do not modify anything else.
acceptance_criteria: ENABLE_ALL=false; all individual flags false; release build strips logs; assembleRelease succeeds
close_reason: Closed

title: Move VLESS/proxy credentials out of Safe.s() into SecretConfigStore
description:
## Problem
Safe.java stores the AES-256 decryption key as four hardcoded byte-array constants (K_PART_1..K_PART_4) at lines 33-40. The matching generate_safe_enc.py also contains the key in plaintext. Anyone who decompiles the APK can trivially recover the key and decrypt every Safe.s() call, including VLESS proxy credentials per CLAUDE.md.

## Files
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/proxy/Safe.java (lines 33-40: hardcoded key)
- generate_safe_enc.py (same key)
- Any file using Safe.s() to store credentials (search for Safe.s( in CameraDaemon.java, AccSentryDaemon.java, SentryDaemon.java)

## What Needs To Change
1. Audit every Safe.s() usage to classify: is this a SECRET (credentials, proxy address) or just an OBFUSCATED STRING (internal service class name, file path)?
2. For any SECRET value: move it to bladewatch_secrets.json (stored via SecretConfigStore) and read it at runtime via SecretConfigStore.getString(). Do NOT leave secrets in Safe.s() calls.
3. For pure obfuscated strings (class names, paths): Safe.s() is acceptable — no change needed.
4. Update generate_safe_enc.py with a comment clarifying it is for non-secret obfuscation only.

## Context
- SecretConfigStore is at app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/SecretConfigStore.kt
- The daemon process (shell UID 2000) can write to the secrets file directly
- The app process uses the TCP command bridge (port 19876) to ask the daemon to write secrets
- CLAUDE.md: 'VLESS proxy credentials use encrypted Safe.s(...) values — use generate_safe_enc.py to encrypt before committing'

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] VLESS proxy address/credentials no longer stored as Safe.s() values in committed source
- [ ] Those values are retrieved from SecretConfigStore at runtime
- [ ] Safe.s() usage for non-secret internal strings is unchanged
- [ ] Build compiles and ./gradlew test passes

Do not make mistakes. Read Safe.java, generate_safe_enc.py, and the affected daemon files fully before editing. Identify which Safe.s() values are credentials vs. obfuscated paths before changing anything. Stop and ask if the classification is ambiguous.
acceptance_criteria: No credential Safe.s() values in source; VLESS/proxy values read from SecretConfigStore; build passes
close_reason: Closed

title: fix: vehicleState data race between poll thread and UI thread loses chargeCap updates
description:
## Context
VehicleController.kt has vehicleState as a plain 'private var VehicleState' with no @Volatile, no AtomicReference, and no synchronization. The BYD DiLink v3 head unit uses a Snapdragon 8155 (8 cores). The field is written from: (1) background poll thread at line 655 via state.copy(chargeCap = vehicleState.chargeCap), (2) main UI thread in DRL/ADAS/charging action handlers (lines 540, 564, 600, 619, 628), (3) VehiclePollInit thread at line 647.

The poll thread's read-modify-write at line 655 is: read vehicleState ref, read .chargeCap off it, write new object back. If the UI thread writes vehicleState between the poll thread's read and write, the poll overwrites the UI's optimistic update. The user sees their stepper tap revert.

## File
app/src/main/java/net/bladewatch/app/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt

## What to do
Move the vehicleState write in the poll loop to the main thread via root.post. In startPolling() (lines 651-657), change:
  val state = client.fetchState() ?: return@scheduleAtFixedRate
  vehicleState = state.copy(chargeCap = vehicleState.chargeCap)
  root.post { if (running.get()) applyStateToViews() }
To:
  val state = client.fetchState() ?: return@scheduleAtFixedRate
  root.post {
    if (running.get()) {
      vehicleState = state.copy(chargeCap = vehicleState.chargeCap)
      applyStateToViews()
    }
  }

Also do the same for the fetchChargeCap write at line 647:
  client.fetchChargeCap()?.let { cap ->
    root.post { vehicleState = vehicleState.copy(chargeCap = cap) }
  }

## Constraints
Do not change the VehicleState data class. Do not change client method signatures. Keep running.get() guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All vehicleState writes happen only on the main thread (root.post or direct UI thread call)
- [ ] No @Volatile needed after the fix (all mutations serialized to main thread)
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug passes

Do not make mistakes. Read VehicleController.kt fully before editing.
close_reason: Closed

title: fix: TripsController distUnit/storType always saved as km/INTERNAL due to GradientDrawable constantState bug
description:

title: Fix VehicleController.vehicleState race condition — add @Volatile
description:
## Problem

VehicleController.vehicleState is a plain var with no @Volatile annotation but is written from two background threads and read from the main thread.

**File:** app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt  
**Line 28:** `private var vehicleState = VehicleState()`  
**Line 647:** `vehicleState = vehicleState.copy(chargeCap = cap)` — written from VehiclePollInit background thread  
**Line 655:** `vehicleState = state.copy(chargeCap = vehicleState.chargeCap)` — written from poll executor thread  
**Main thread reads:** applyStateToViews() and all buildXxxTab() methods read vehicleState directly

Under concurrent load the main thread may see a stale or partially-updated reference.

## Fix

Add `@Volatile` to the declaration:
```kotlin
@Volatile private var vehicleState = VehicleState()
```

Or for stronger safety: change the background writes to go through root.post {} so all vehicleState mutations happen on the main thread (consistent with how applyStateToViews() already works).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No other bare background-thread writes to vehicleState exist

title: Fix LiveStreamClient.stop() blocking main thread — move join() off UI thread
description:
## Problem

LiveStreamClient.stop() calls worker?.join(2_000L) which blocks the calling thread. The call chain is:

LiveViewFragment.onPause() [main thread]  
→ controller.onPause() [main thread]  
→ streamClient.stop() [main thread]  
→ worker?.join(2_000L) [BLOCKS main thread up to 2s]

**File:** app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/liveview/LiveStreamClient.kt  
**Lines 58-64:** stop() function

If activeSocket.close() doesn't promptly unblock the stream reader (OS-level socket teardown delay), the main thread is frozen for up to 2 seconds. This causes visible jank during fragment navigation.

## Fix

Move the join off the calling thread. Change stop() to:
```kotlin
fun stop() {
    running.set(false)
    runCatching { activeSocket?.close() }
    val w = worker
    worker = null
    Thread({ w?.join(2_000L); releaseCodec() }, "LiveStop").apply { isDaemon = true; start() }
}
```

Remove releaseCodec() from the end of runStream()'s finally block since the thread now handles it. Ensure no double-release.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] stop() returns immediately without blocking the calling thread
- [ ] MediaCodec is still released after the worker exits
- [ ] No double-release of codec or socket
- [ ] Build passes (./gradlew assembleDebug)

Do not make mistakes. Read LiveStreamClient.kt and LiveViewController.kt fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing.

title: Investigate H264CircularBuffer: 0 keyframes and oversized packet drops
description:
## Problem
The cam_daemon.log shows two recurring H264 buffer issues:

  H264CircularBuffer: Dropping oversized packet (size=527418 > 262144)
  H264CircularBuffer: Buffer state: 155 packets, 10.0 sec, 0 keyframes, pool=32 free

The buffer has 155 packets spanning 10 seconds but zero keyframes. Video saved during this state would not be seekable and may not decode correctly. Oversized packets (>262144 bytes) are being silently dropped.

## Root Cause to Find
- Locate H264CircularBuffer implementation (likely in app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ or camera/ subdirectory)
- Why are 0 keyframes occurring? Is the camera encoder not producing IDR frames at the expected interval? Check camera encoding config (keyframe interval / I-frame interval setting).
- Is the 262144 byte max packet size appropriate for the current bitrate/resolution? A single 527418-byte packet suggests a large I-frame is being dropped — which explains the 0 keyframes.
- Is there a relationship between the oversized packet drops and the 0-keyframe state? (i.e. the I-frame is being dropped because it is too large, so the buffer never gets a keyframe)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause of 0 keyframes identified
- [ ] Packet size limit reviewed against actual encoder output sizes
- [ ] Fix proposed: either increase MAX_PACKET_SIZE or reduce encoder bitrate/resolution so I-frames fit
- [ ] After fix, buffer state shows >0 keyframes in logcat within 30 seconds of camera start

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Increased MAX_PACKET_SIZE from 256KB to 768KB in H264CircularBuffer.java:31. Root cause: camera configured at BITRATE=4Mbps, KEYFRAME_INTERVAL=2s, 5120x960@25fps produces I-frames up to 527KB which exceeded 256KB limit. Buffer dropped all I-frames as oversized, resulting in 0 keyframes. New 768KB threshold handles STANDARD-H.264 comfortably through PREMIUM typical I-frames. Pool ceiling 200 x 768KB = 150MB peak.

title: Implement storage priority: SD card → USB → internal for recordings and settings
description:
## Context

BladeWatch currently defaults to internal storage for recordings and settings. The device may have an SD card or external USB drive attached. We should prefer external storage when available, both for capacity reasons and so that footage survives a head-unit reboot/crash without filling internal storage.

## What needs to be done

On daemon startup, implement a storage priority scan:

1. Check for an SD card mount point (e.g. `/storage/sdcard1`, `/mnt/media_rw/`, or any mount under `/storage/` that is not `emulated`)
2. If not found, check for an external USB drive (e.g. `/mnt/usb*`, `/storage/usb*`)
3. Fall back to internal storage (`/storage/emulated/0`)

For each candidate mount point:
- Verify it is mounted and writable
- Check if a `BladeWatch/` folder exists; if so, prefer that drive immediately
- If no `BladeWatch/` folder exists, create one before adopting that drive
- Once a drive is selected, persist the resolved base path in the unified config so all subsystems (recordings, surveillance, proximity, trips) use it

Update the following subsystems to use the resolved storage base path instead of the hard-coded internal path:
- Recording output paths in `CameraDaemon.java`
- Settings/config persistence paths in `UnifiedConfigManager.kt`
- Any other path constants referencing `/storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch`

Relevant files to read before editing:
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/SecretConfigStore.kt`
- `docs/data-flow-and-storage.md`

## Constraints

- Do NOT change the IPC token path (`/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token`) or config/secrets paths under `/data/local/tmp/` — those must stay on tmpfs
- The scan must be fast (< 200 ms) so it does not delay daemon startup
- If no external storage is found, silently fall through to internal — no error, no crash
- If the selected drive is later unmounted mid-session, log a warning but do not crash; new recordings can fall back to internal
- This is a daemon-side change only; no UI work is required in this task

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On startup with an SD card present containing a `BladeWatch/` folder, recordings go to the SD card
- [ ] On startup with an SD card present but no `BladeWatch/` folder, the folder is created and recordings go to the SD card
- [ ] With no SD card but a USB drive present, same logic applies to USB
- [ ] With neither SD nor USB, recordings go to internal storage as before
- [ ] `docs/data-flow-and-storage.md` is updated to document the new priority order
- [ ] Unit test or integration note documents the expected behavior

## Warning

Do not make mistakes. Read every referenced file fully before editing. Verify the build compiles (`./gradlew assembleDebug`) and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added applyAutoStoragePriority() to StorageManager.java with USB drive discovery. Called from CameraDaemon.java startup after fixAllPermissions(). Runs unconditionally on every boot: SD card first, then USB, then internal. Docs updated in data-flow-and-storage.md. Build: SUCCESS.

title: Migrate remaining raw-HTTP/TCP screens to Connect gRPC (Dashboard, MainActivity, Diagnostics)
description:

title: Auto-commit hook bundles .beads Dolt backups into source commits (violates no-auto-commit rule)
description:
## Problem
CLAUDE.md states: "Do not run git add/commit/push automatically. All commits are reviewed and made manually by the developer." But during the recent session, after running bd close, a commit (a25e1dc "Add content-type negotiation tests, enhance wire parity tests, and implement recording mode API") was created automatically WITHOUT an explicit git commit. It bundled the source changes together with a large sweep of .beads/backup/*.darc Dolt database files. After bd close, git status reads clean and the work is already in HEAD, which is surprising and conflates DB state with source.

There is also .gitignore churn around .beads (an earlier bd auto-export warned that .beads is gitignored, yet .beads/backup files landed in this commit).

## Investigation / Steps
1. Identify what auto-commits on bd close: check for a Claude Code hook in .claude/settings.json / settings.local.json, a beads/Dolt post-action hook, or a git hook (.git/hooks). Look for anything invoking git add/commit tied to bd operations.
2. Decide the intended behavior with the developer: either (a) disable auto-commit entirely to honor the manual-commit rule, or (b) scope it so it NEVER stages source files and NEVER bundles .beads Dolt backups with code.
3. Fix .gitignore so .beads tracking is consistent: decide whether .beads/ (and .beads/backup/) should be tracked or ignored, and make check-ignore agree with reality (currently inconsistent — bd auto-export complained .beads is ignored while .beads/backup got committed).
4. If desired, split commit a25e1dc so the .beads backup sweep is separated from the source changes (developer decision; do not rewrite shared history without approval).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Source of the auto-commit identified and documented in this issue.
- [ ] bd close (and other bd ops) no longer auto-commit source files, OR auto-commit is scoped to beads data only and never mixes with code — per developer decision.
- [ ] .gitignore and git check-ignore agree on whether .beads/backup is tracked; no more auto-export "ignored by .gitignore" warnings.
- [ ] Documented in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md so future sessions know the commit model.

## Constraints
- Do NOT rewrite or force-push shared history without explicit developer approval.
- Do not delete beads data.

Do not make mistakes. Investigate the hook source before changing anything. Confirm the desired commit model with the developer if ambiguous rather than guessing. Do not force-push.
close_reason: Root cause: previous session ran git add . violating CLAUDE.md manual-commit rule. Fix: (1) Added .beads/backup/*.darc and .beads/backup/oldgen/ to .gitignore so darc chunks can never be accidentally staged. (2) Added Beads commit model note to CLAUDE.md git workflow section documenting never to use git add . and what is/is not tracked. .darc files confirmed ignored via git check-ignore.

title: SetConfig false-boolean toggle completeness: guard against omitted-scalar persistence bugs
description:
## Problem
JSON serialization omits false/zero scalars on the wire. SurveillanceServiceImpl.SetConfig (~lines 60-82) compensates by re-adding a fixed CONFIG_BOOLEAN_TOGGLES list (detectPerson, detectCar, detectBike, nightMode, cameraFront/Right/Rear/Left) before forwarding to the REST handler, because the REST handler reads toggles with has()-gating and would otherwise keep the old value. Any NEW boolean toggle not added to that list will silently fail to persist its OFF state. The same omitted-scalar hazard applies to other Set* RPCs whose REST handler reads booleans/zero-values via has().

## Files
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/SurveillanceServiceImpl.java (~lines 60-82, CONFIG_BOOLEAN_TOGGLES)
- Audit other Set* impls: SettingsServiceImpl, StorageServiceImpl, StreamServiceImpl, TripsServiceImpl, VehicleServiceImpl

## Steps
1. Verify CONFIG_BOOLEAN_TOGGLES matches the full set of boolean fields in SetConfigRequest / surveillance config proto (compare against proto/bladewatch/v1/surveillance.proto).
2. Audit each other Set* RPC: if its REST handler reads a boolean/int via has()/optional gating and the proto field can legitimately be false/0, ensure the impl re-adds the field (or the REST handler is changed to treat absent as false).
3. Prefer a robust approach: derive the toggle list from the proto descriptor rather than a hand-maintained string array, so new fields are covered automatically.

## Acceptance criteria

title: Contract test: REST JSON -> Connect proto field parity (catch silent json_name drops)
description:
## Problem
Connect responses are produced by shelling the REST handlers and re-parsing JSON with JsonFormat.ignoringUnknownFields(). Any REST key that does not match the proto canonical/json_name silently drops to a default, with no error -> empty/zero fields in the UI. Commit 54653bb fixed a batch, but the pattern re-introduces silent data loss on any future REST handler rename. Add a guard test.

## Files

  - RecordingsServiceImpl (GetStats: normalCount->recordingsCount, sentrySize->surveillanceSizeBytes, etc.)
  - SurveillanceServiceImpl (GetStatus: nested status.active->pipelineRunning, status.enabled->surveillanceActive)
  - SettingsServiceImpl (SetQuality: recordingBitrate->recordingQuality, note->message)
  - TripsServiceImpl (telemetry/summary/range JSON-string blobs; GpsTrace [[lat,lon]]->{lat,lon})

## Steps
1. For each high-reshape RPC, capture a representative REST JSON payload (from docs/http-api-reference.md or a recorded daemon response).
2. Run it through the Connect impl mapping and parse into the proto with the SAME JsonFormat config the client uses (ignoringUnknownFields).
3. Assert every field the Android/Angular client actually reads is non-default after parsing (i.e. nothing silently dropped).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Renaming a REST key (or a proto json_name) makes the test fail.

title: Fix: TripsServiceImpl.cachedHandler is a data race (not volatile, unsynchronized check-then-act)
description:
## Problem

TripsServiceImpl has a shared mutable field with a check-then-act pattern that is not thread-safe:

  private TripApiHandler cachedHandler;  // line 37 — not volatile, not synchronized

  private ConnectResponse invoke(...) {
      ...
      if (cachedHandler == null) {          // line 75 — read without lock
          cachedHandler = new TripApiHandler(tam);  // line 76 — write without lock
      }
      TripApiHandler handler = cachedHandler;  // line 78 — misleading local alias
      ...
  }

HttpServer uses a 32-thread fixed thread pool (Executors.newFixedThreadPool(32)). TripsServiceImpl is a single instance registered once with ConnectDispatcher. Two or more threads can call invoke() simultaneously, both observe cachedHandler == null, and both allocate a TripApiHandler. Due to lack of volatile, the JMM does not guarantee that a write by thread A is visible to thread B, potentially causing repeated redundant allocations.

The local variable 'handler' at line 78 looks like the classic DCL idiom but provides no memory visibility guarantee without volatile on the field.

Currently the TripApiHandler constructor does only 'this.manager = manager' with no side effects, so no resource leak occurs — but this is fragile and relies on constructor internals.

## Fix

Make cachedHandler volatile (sufficient for a single-field publish-once pattern):
  private volatile TripApiHandler cachedHandler;

Or use an AtomicReference:
  private final AtomicReference<TripApiHandler> cachedHandler = new AtomicReference<>();

The null-check pattern is fine for lazy initialization if the field is volatile (the write will be seen by all subsequent reads). The local variable alias can be removed as it adds no value.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/TripsServiceImpl.java (lines 37, 75-78)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] cachedHandler field is volatile or AtomicReference
- [ ] The local variable 'handler' alias is removed (use cachedHandler directly)
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read TripsServiceImpl.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: AuthServiceImpl hardcodes rate-limit identity 'connect': per-IP login throttle defeated + global lockout DoS
description:
Connect login uses a single shared rate-limit bucket, defeating per-IP brute-force protection and letting one attacker lock out all legitimate Connect logins.

DETAIL: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/AuthServiceImpl.java handleLogin (~line 28) passes the literal constant 'connect' as the rateLimitIdentity to AuthApiHandler.handle. The real HTTP path (HttpServer.java ~line 369-377) derives a per-client identity from X-Forwarded-For else the socket address. AuthApiHandler keys lockout state on identity via rateLimits.computeIfAbsent(identity,...) (~line 87) and checkRateLimit/clearRateLimit (~line 98-103). With the fixed 'connect' key, all Connect logins share one RateLimitBucket: 10 failed attempts trip the 30s lockout for EVERY Connect login (DoS), and per-IP throttling is fully collapsed.

FIX: Thread the real client identity (X-Forwarded-For / remote address) from the HttpServer request context through ConnectDispatcher to AuthServiceImpl.handleLogin, and pass it as the rate-limit identity — matching the REST path.

FILES: server/connect/impl/AuthServiceImpl.java, server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java, server/connect/ConnectServiceHandler.java (handler signature may need the client identity), HttpServer.java (pass remote identity into dispatch).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] Connect login rate-limiting is keyed per client IP, matching the REST /auth/token path.
- [ ] One client hitting the lockout does not lock out other clients.
- [ ] Build compiles (./gradlew assembleDebug) and AuthManagerTest/AuthMiddlewareTest pass.

title: TripsServiceImpl.invoke() drops _status: REST 404/500 errors masked as Connect 200 success
description:
Trip RPC error responses (e.g. 'Trip not found' 404) are delivered to the client as Connect HTTP 200 success bodies, so the web UI treats a missing trip as found.

DETAIL: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/TripsServiceImpl.java invoke() (~line 73-78) calls TripApiHandler.handleRequest, then unconditionally does result.remove("_status") and returns result.toString() as a Connect success — it never inspects the status. TripApiHandler.errorResponse() (~line 825-835) builds errors as {"success":false,"error":message,"_status":status}; e.g. missing trip returns errorResponse('Trip not found', 404) (~line 198). Because invoke() strips _status without branching, the dispatcher emits HTTP 200 with a body that looks successful.

FIX: invoke() must read _status BEFORE removing it; when _status indicates an error (>=400), throw an appropriate ConnectException (mapping 404->not_found, 400->invalid_argument, 410->not_found/failed_precondition, 500->internal) so the dispatcher returns the correct Connect error instead of a fake success.

NOTE: also relevant to the separate task about ConnectDispatcher mapping all errors to HTTP 400 — coordinate the code->status mapping.

FILES: server/connect/impl/TripsServiceImpl.java, server/connect/ConnectException.java, the REST TripApiHandler (read-only, to confirm _status values).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] A GetTrip for a non-existent id returns a Connect error (not_found), not a 200 success.
- [ ] All TripsService methods that go through invoke() propagate _status as Connect errors.
- [ ] Successful trip responses still return 200 with the body and no _status field.
- [ ] Build compiles (./gradlew assembleDebug).

title: ConnectHandlerUtil.capture() force-parses body as JSONObject: breaks binary snapshots and non-object/error bodies
description:
The Connect adapter assumes every wrapped REST handler returns exactly one JSON object, so it throws on binary or non-object responses, turning real responses/errors into opaque 'internal' Connect errors.

DETAIL: ConnectHandlerUtil.capture() (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java ~line 36-42) does new JSONObject(body) unconditionally and wraps any exception as ConnectException('internal','Handler failed: ...').

CASE 1 (CONFIRMED, binary): SurveillanceServiceImpl.handleGetSnapshot (server/connect/impl/SurveillanceServiceImpl.java ~line 75-86) wraps SurveillanceApiHandler which writes raw image/jpeg bytes (SurveillanceApiHandler sendQuadrantSnapshot/sendQuadrantFromMosaic ~line 1222-1278). new JSONObject(<binary jpeg>) throws → GetSnapshot ALWAYS returns internal error; ROI snapshots never load (surveillance.component.ts getSnapshot expects resp.imageJpeg bytes). NOTE: GetHeatmap is fine — sendHeatmap returns JSON via HttpResponse.sendJson (~line 1150).

CASE 2 (general): any wrapped handler that returns a top-level JSON ARRAY, an empty body, or an HTML/redirect (e.g. internal 401) throws the same way, masking the real status/payload.

FIX DIRECTION: Connect responses that carry binary need a bytes pass-through path (don't parse JPEG as JSON) — map the JPEG bytes into the GetSnapshotResponse.imageJpeg field. For non-object JSON, tolerate arrays/scalars or wrap appropriately. Centralize so all 12 ServiceImpls benefit.

FILES: server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java, server/connect/impl/SurveillanceServiceImpl.java, proto/bladewatch/v1/surveillance.proto (GetSnapshotResponse), web/src/app/pages/surveillance/surveillance.component.ts.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] GetSnapshot returns the JPEG bytes successfully through Connect and the surveillance page renders the snapshot.
- [ ] A wrapped handler returning a JSON array or non-object body does not throw an opaque internal error.
- [ ] GetHeatmap still works (regression check).
- [ ] Build compiles (./gradlew assembleDebug).

title: Add Gradle task to build Angular UI and serve from HttpServer
description:
Add Gradle automation to build the Angular app and update HttpServer to serve the Angular dist output.

## Context
Phase 3 web UI migration (BladeWatch-axc). Depends on Angular scaffold (BladeWatch-nvs).

## Two parts

### Part 1: Gradle task in app/build.gradle.kts
tasks.register<Exec>("buildAngularWebUI") {
    group = "build"
    description = "Build the Angular web UI and copy to assets"
    workingDir = file("../web")
    commandLine("npm", "run", "build")
    doLast {
        copy {
            from("../web/dist")
            into("src/main/assets/web/angular")
        }
    }
}
// Make the Android build depend on this:
tasks.named("generateDebugAssets") { dependsOn("buildAngularWebUI") }
tasks.named("generateReleaseAssets") { dependsOn("buildAngularWebUI") }

Add .gitignore entry: app/src/main/assets/web/angular/ (generated at build time)

### Part 2: HttpServer changes to serve Angular
In app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.java:

- Requests to /app/* or /* (when no specific route matches) serve files from the angular/ web asset directory instead of local/
- The Angular app's index.html is served for any unmatched path (SPA fallback routing)

- The existing /api/*, /auth/*, /video/*, /thumb/*, /ws, /status, and /bladewatch.v1.* routes take priority over the SPA fallback

Keep the old local/ pages accessible at /legacy/* temporarily (for regression testing), then remove in a follow-up.

- [ ] API calls from Angular (Connect protocol, /api/*) still work

title: Implement ConnectProvider and auth interceptor for Angular
description:
Create the core Angular provider that builds the ConnectRPC transport, injects JWT auth, and provides typed service clients to the DI system.

## Context
Phase 3 web UI migration (BladeWatch-axc). Depends on buf TypeScript codegen task. All Angular page components depend on this.

## Files to create
web/src/app/core/connect/
  connect.provider.ts
  auth.interceptor.ts
  connect-clients.ts

### connect.provider.ts
Provides a transport factory using createConnectTransport from @connectrpc/connect-web:
  export function provideConnect(): EnvironmentProviders {
    return makeEnvironmentProviders([
      { provide: CONNECT_TRANSPORT, useFactory: () => createConnectTransport({ baseUrl: environment.apiBaseUrl }) }
    ])
  }

- environment.apiBaseUrl = '' (empty string = relative, routes through Vite proxy in dev; direct loopback in production WebView)

### auth.interceptor.ts
A ConnectRPC interceptor (not Angular HTTP interceptor) that:
1. Reads the byd_session cookie
2. Injects it as Authorization: Bearer <jwt> on every Connect request
3. On 401/permission_denied response, emits a redirect-to-login event

Connect interceptors: https://connectrpc.com/docs/web/interceptors

### connect-clients.ts
Injectable services that wrap createPromiseClient(ServiceType, transport):
  @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
  export class ConnectClients {
    readonly auth: PromiseClient<typeof AuthService>
    readonly recordings: PromiseClient<typeof RecordingsService>
    readonly surveillance: PromiseClient<typeof SurveillanceService>
    readonly safeLocations: PromiseClient<typeof SafeLocationsService>
    readonly stream: PromiseClient<typeof StreamService>
    readonly vehicle: PromiseClient<typeof VehicleService>
    readonly storage: PromiseClient<typeof StorageService>
    readonly trips: PromiseClient<typeof TripsService>
    readonly settings: PromiseClient<typeof SettingsService>
    readonly updates: PromiseClient<typeof UpdateService>
    readonly notifications: PromiseClient<typeof NotificationsService>
    readonly system: PromiseClient<typeof SystemService>
  }

Register provideConnect() in app.config.ts providers array.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ConnectClients injectable and resolves in Angular DI
- [ ] TypeScript compiles (tsc --noEmit passes)
- [ ] npm run build succeeds
- [ ] Auth interceptor reads byd_session cookie and injects Bearer header (verify with browser devtools in dev mode)

Do not create page components yet. Read @connectrpc/connect-web docs for createConnectTransport and interceptor API.

title: Implement ConnectDispatcher base class and routing
description:
Implement the core Connect protocol dispatcher that routes HTTP requests to service implementations inside the existing HttpServer.

## Context
Sub-task of BladeWatch-xxj. Depends on generated proto stubs (BladeWatch-9xw). This is the foundation all service impls plug into.

## What to build
New file: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java

### Responsibilities
1. Match incoming HTTP requests with path pattern: /bladewatch.v1.{ServiceName}/{MethodName}
2. Validate Content-Type: application/connect+json (return 415 if wrong)
3. Validate Connect-Protocol-Version: 1 header (return 400 if missing/wrong)
4. Read request body as UTF-8 JSON string
5. Look up service + method in a registry (Map<String, ConnectServiceHandler>)
6. Return 404 Connect error if service/method not found
7. Invoke service handler — pass raw JSON request body, get JSON response body back
8. Write 200 response with Content-Type: application/connect+json

### ConnectServiceHandler interface
New file: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectServiceHandler.java

public interface ConnectServiceHandler {
    // Returns JSON response string. Throws ConnectException on error.
    String handle(String requestJson) throws ConnectException;
}

### ConnectException
New file: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectException.java

Carries a Connect error code (string) and message. Codes:
- invalid_argument
- not_found
- permission_denied
- unavailable
- internal
- unimplemented

### Connect error response format
{"code": "not_found", "message": "Service not registered: bladewatch.v1.FooService"}

### Registration helper
ConnectDispatcher.register(String serviceFqn, String methodName, ConnectServiceHandler handler)

### Integration in HttpServer
In HttpServer.java, add a check before the existing route dispatch:
  if (path.startsWith("/bladewatch.v1.")) {
      connectDispatcher.dispatch(exchange);
      return;
  }

Auth middleware runs first (before this check) — no changes to AuthMiddleware needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ConnectServiceHandler.java and ConnectException.java created
- [ ] /bladewatch.v1.Foo/Bar returns 404 Connect error (no service registered)
- [ ] Missing Connect-Protocol-Version returns 400 Connect error
- [ ] Wrong Content-Type returns 415
- [ ] assembleDebug compiles

Do not make mistakes. Read HttpServer.java and AuthMiddleware.java before editing. Do not modify existing route handlers. Verify assembleDebug compiles before closing.

title: Build Angular + Vite web UI with ConnectRPC TypeScript client
description:
Rebuild the web UI as an Angular SPA using Vite as the build tool and @connectrpc/connect for all API calls. This replaces the existing plain JS/HTML pages in app/src/main/assets/web/local/.

## Context
Phase 3 of BladeWatch-5zy. Depends on BladeWatch-9xw (proto/buf setup), BladeWatch-t6m (proto schemas), and the Connect server being live (BladeWatch-xxj). The Angular app replaces the current static HTML pages but the shared/ assets (video decoders, vendor libs) remain.

## Why Angular + Vite (not raw JS)
The existing web UI is plain ES modules with no build step. Angular gives us TypeScript safety, reactive change detection, and proper component boundaries. Vite gives fast HMR during development and optimized production bundles. The ConnectRPC TypeScript client integrates natively with TypeScript.

## Project scaffold
Location: web/ (new directory at repo root, sibling of app/)
  web/
    angular.json
    vite.config.ts
    tsconfig.json
    package.json
    src/
      app/
        app.component.ts
        app.routes.ts
        core/
          auth/          auth.service.ts, auth.guard.ts
          connect/       connect.provider.ts  (builds PromiseClient instances)
          services/      (one .service.ts per ConnectRPC service, 12 total)
        pages/
          dashboard/     (maps to current index.html)
          recording/     (maps to recording.html)
          surveillance/  (maps to surveillance.html)
          events/        (maps to events.html)
          trips/         (maps to trips.html)
          vehicle/       (maps to vehicle-control.html)
          notifications/ (maps to notifications.html)
          performance/   (maps to performance.html)
          about/         (maps to about.html)
          login/         (maps to login.html)
        shared/          (reusable Angular components)
      assets/            (static assets, copied from app/src/main/assets/web/shared/ as needed)
      environments/      (environment.ts with API base URL)

## Angular + build dependencies (package.json)
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@angular/core": "^19.x",
    "@angular/common": "^19.x",
    "@angular/router": "^19.x",
    "@angular/platform-browser": "^19.x",
    "@angular/forms": "^19.x",

    "@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es": "^2.x",
    "@connectrpc/protoc-gen-connect-es": "^2.x"
  }
}

Use @analogjs/vite-plugin-angular (Analog framework plugin) to integrate Angular with Vite.

## buf.gen.yaml — TypeScript output (add alongside existing Java/Kotlin output)
- plugin: buf.build/bufbuild/es
  out: ../web/src/gen
  opt: target=ts
- plugin: buf.build/connectrpc/es
  out: ../web/src/gen

Generated output goes to web/src/gen/ (committed to repo).

## ConnectProvider (core/connect/connect.provider.ts)
- Reads base URL from environment: http://127.0.0.1:8080 (dev) or relative (prod)
- Creates a ConnectTransport using createConnectTransport({baseUrl, interceptors: [authInterceptor]})
- authInterceptor reads JWT from cookie byd_session and injects as Authorization: Bearer header
- Exports createClient(ServiceType) helper used by each service

## Service layer (core/services/)
One Angular injectable service per proto service:
- AuthApiService → AuthService
- RecordingsApiService → RecordingsService
- SurveillanceApiService → SurveillanceService

- TripsApiService → TripsService
- SettingsApiService → SettingsService
- UpdateApiService → UpdateService
- NotificationsApiService → NotificationsService

Each service wraps PromiseClient calls and maps to Angular Observables (using from() or rxjs).

## Pages
Each page component reproduces the feature set of the existing HTML page it replaces:
- Dashboard: system status, live stream, camera selector, battery/ACC/range
- Recording: recording list, filter, video playback, delete
- Surveillance: enable/disable toggle, config sliders, snapshot preview, safe zones

The WebSocket H.264 stream is NOT migrated. The dashboard page embeds a canvas element and uses the existing SotaPlayer from shared/SotaPlayer.js by loading it as a vanilla script asset. The Angular component initializes it after view init.

## Auth flow

title: Migrate Android app to use connect-kotlin generated stubs
description:
Replace HTTP REST calls in the Android app with generated ConnectRPC Kotlin stubs.

## Context
Phase 2 of BladeWatch-5zy. Depends on BladeWatch-9xw (code gen setup) and the parallel server being live. The daemon must be running the Connect endpoints before testing this.

## Files to migrate (Android-side clients)
These files currently use DaemonHttpClient (HTTP REST) and should be migrated to use connect-kotlin:

1. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/util/DaemonHttpClient.kt
   → Keep for now (used by legacy callers), but add ConnectClientProvider.kt alongside it as the new preferred client

2. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/recording/RecordingSettingsClient.kt
   → Migrate to RecordingsServiceClient (generated stub)

3. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsClient.kt
   → Migrate to SurveillanceServiceClient + SafeLocationsServiceClient

4. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/trips/TripsClient.kt
   → Migrate to TripsServiceClient

5. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleClient.kt
   → Migrate to VehicleServiceClient

6. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/liveview/LiveStreamClient.kt
   → Migrate Stream quality/enable/disable calls to StreamServiceClient
   → WebSocket streaming itself stays unchanged

## Dependencies to add to app/build.gradle.kts
implementation("com.connectrpc:connect-kotlin:0.6.0")
implementation("com.connectrpc:connect-kotlin-okhttp:0.6.0")
implementation("com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp:4.12.0")

## ConnectClientProvider.kt
New file: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/client/ConnectClientProvider.kt

Singleton that builds and caches the OkHttpClient + ProtocolClientInterface:
- Base URL: http://127.0.0.1:8080 (CameraDaemon.HTTP_PORT)
- Proxy.NO_PROXY (same as DaemonHttpClient)
- JWT injected as Authorization: Bearer header via OkHttp interceptor
  → Use AuthManager.generateJwt() with same caching logic as DaemonHttpClient
- Protocol: ConnectHttpInterceptor (Connect protocol over HTTP/1.1)
- Timeout: 5s connect, 10s read

## Migration pattern for each client
Before (DaemonHttpClient REST):
  val conn = DaemonHttpClient.open("/api/recordings?filter=ALL", "GET")
  val body = conn.inputStream.bufferedReader().readText()
  val json = JSONObject(body)

After (connect-kotlin):
  val client = ConnectClientProvider.recordingsService()
  val response = client.listRecordings(ListRecordingsRequest { filter = RecordingFilter.ALL })
  // response.success { it.recordings } or response.failure { it.error }

## Coroutine integration
connect-kotlin uses suspend functions by default. Existing clients likely use threads/handlers.
- Wrap connect-kotlin calls in CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO)
- Propagate results to the main thread via LiveData or callback (match existing pattern in each file)
- Do NOT change the external interface of each client class (other code depends on it)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ConnectClientProvider.kt created and builds
- [ ] RecordingSettingsClient migrated — recordings load in UI
- [ ] SurveillanceSettingsClient migrated — surveillance config loads and saves
- [ ] TripsClient migrated — trips list loads
- [ ] VehicleClient migrated — lock/unlock/flash actions work
- [ ] LiveStreamClient migrated for quality/status calls
- [ ] assembleDebug compiles with no errors
- [ ] App installed on device (192.168.0.251:5555) — all migrated features work

Do not make mistakes. Read each client file fully before migrating. Read AuthManager.java and DaemonHttpClient.kt for the JWT caching pattern. Do not change public method signatures of client classes. Verify assembleDebug compiles. Install and test on device before closing.

title: Implement ConnectDispatcher and service impls in HttpServer (Phase 1)
description:
Add Connect protocol routing to the existing HttpServer.java and implement all 12 service handler classes that wrap the existing REST handler logic.

## Context
Phase 1 of BladeWatch-5zy. Depends on BladeWatch-t6m (proto schemas) and BladeWatch-9xw (code gen). The existing REST endpoints on port 8080 must remain fully functional — this adds a parallel path only.

## What the Connect protocol looks like over HTTP/1.1
A Connect unary request is:
  POST /bladewatch.v1.RecordingsService/ListRecordings HTTP/1.1
  Content-Type: application/connect+json
  Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
  Connect-Protocol-Version: 1

  {"filter": "ALL"}

A success response is:
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  Content-Type: application/connect+json

  {"recordings": [...]}

An error response is:
  HTTP/1.1 400/500 OK
  Content-Type: application/connect+json

  {"code": "invalid_argument", "message": "..."}

Note: Connect protocol error codes are string codes (not HTTP status codes).
Reference: https://connectrpc.com/docs/protocol

## Changes to HttpServer.java
File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.java

1. Add a route match for paths starting with /bladewatch.v1. — route to ConnectDispatcher
2. Auth middleware already runs before routing — no changes needed there
3. The ConnectDispatcher reads:
   - The path to determine service + method
   - Content-Type: must be application/connect+json (return 415 if not)
   - Connect-Protocol-Version header: must be "1"
   - Request body as JSON → parse into generated protobuf message
4. Dispatch to the correct service implementation method
5. Serialize the protobuf response to JSON → write as 200 OK

## ConnectDispatcher class
New file: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java

- Takes a Map<String, ConnectService> registry (service FQDN → impl)
- Reads path: /bladewatch.v1.{ServiceName}/{MethodName}
- Parses request JSON using protobuf-java-util JsonFormat
- Invokes the correct method
- Serializes response using JsonFormat
- Wraps Connect error codes on exception

## Service implementation classes (12 total)
New directory: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/

For each service, create a class that:
1. Accepts the generated request proto message
2. Delegates to the EXISTING handler (e.g., RecordingsApiHandler) or business logic
3. Returns the generated response proto message

The service impls MUST NOT duplicate business logic — they are thin adapters.

Example: RecordingsServiceImpl.listRecordings(ListRecordingsRequest req) {
  // call RecordingsApiHandler.getRecordingsList(req.getFilter().name())
  // build ListRecordingsResponse from result
  return response
}

Services to implement (maps to existing handlers):
- AuthServiceImpl → AuthApiHandler
- RecordingsServiceImpl → RecordingsApiHandler
- SurveillanceServiceImpl → SurveillanceApiHandler
- SafeLocationsServiceImpl → SafeLocationApiHandler
- StreamServiceImpl → StreamingApiHandler
- VehicleServiceImpl → VehicleControlApiHandler + GpsApiHandler
- StorageServiceImpl → FormatStorageApiHandler + ExternalStorageApiHandler
- TripsServiceImpl → TripApiHandler
- SettingsServiceImpl → QualitySettingsApiHandler
- UpdateServiceImpl → UpdateApiHandler
- NotificationsServiceImpl → NotificationApiHandler
- SystemServiceImpl → PerformanceApiHandler + AudioTestApiHandler + ModelsApiHandler + status logic

## Connect error code mapping
Java exception → Connect error code:
- IllegalArgumentException → invalid_argument
- SecurityException → permission_denied
- FileNotFoundException / NoSuchElementException → not_found
- IOException → unavailable
- UnsupportedOperationException → unimplemented
- Any other → internal

## Registration in HttpServer
In HttpServer constructor or init method:
  connectDispatcher = new ConnectDispatcher(Map.of(
    "bladewatch.v1.AuthService", new AuthServiceImpl(authManager),
    "bladewatch.v1.RecordingsService", new RecordingsServiceImpl(recordingsHandler),
    ...
  ));

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ConnectDispatcher routes correctly to all 12 services
- [ ] curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/bladewatch.v1.SystemService/GetStatus -H 'Content-Type: application/connect+json' -H 'Connect-Protocol-Version: 1' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <jwt>' -d '{}' returns valid JSON
- [ ] All existing REST endpoints still return correct responses (no regression)
- [ ] Connect error format returned on invalid requests
- [ ] Auth failure returns Connect error code permission_denied
- [ ] assembleDebug build compiles

Do not make mistakes. Read HttpServer.java, AuthMiddleware.java, and each existing ApiHandler fully before writing any code. Do not modify any existing handler logic. Verify assembleDebug compiles before closing.

title: Epic: Migrate REST endpoints to ConnectRPC
description:
Migrate all ~50 HTTP REST endpoints to the Connect protocol (ConnectRPC) in three phases: (1) parallel Connect server alongside existing REST, (2) Android app migration, (3) web UI migration.

## Why
The existing REST API is implicit JSON with no schema enforcement. ConnectRPC gives us type-safe protobuf schemas, code generation for all clients, and a standard protocol that works over HTTP/1.1 (critical for the WebView client and loopback).

## Scope
- 12 services, ~45 unary RPCs
- Wire protocol: Connect protocol over HTTP/1.1 (not raw gRPC) — no HTTP/2 server required
- WebSocket streaming (/ws) is explicitly OUT of scope
- TCP command server (19876) and Surveillance IPC (19877) are OUT of scope

## Phases
Phase 1 – Parallel server: proto schemas + buf setup + ConnectDispatcher in HttpServer + service impls

title: Persist PerformanceMonitor snapshots to rotating CSV/JSONL
description:
GOAL: Make performance data survive beyond the live dashboard. Today PerformanceMonitor polls /proc and /sys/class/kgsl at 1 Hz, keeps only 60 samples in memory, and only runs while a WebView client is connected — so perf data is lost on disconnect and cannot be analyzed post-hoc.

CONTEXT / FILES TO READ FULLY FIRST:
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/PerformanceMonitor.java (the collector; snapshot struct has cpuUsagePercent, appCpuUsagePercent, cpuFreqMhz, cpuTempCelsius, memUsedMb, memUsagePercent, appMemoryMb, gpuFreqMhz, gpuUsagePercent)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/logging/DebugAppLogger.kt (reference implementation for rotating file writes: size limit, rotation count, naming .1/.2/.3, synchronized writes, atomic-ish append)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt (isTimingLogsEnabled / isDebugLogsEnabled toggle to gate persistence)

STEPS:
1. Add an optional persistence sink to PerformanceMonitor that appends each collected snapshot to a rotating file at /storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/performance.csv (or .jsonl). Prefer CSV with a header row for easy analysis; one row per snapshot with epoch-millis timestamp + all snapshot fields.
2. Reuse the rotation approach from DebugAppLogger.kt (max ~5MB per file, keep 3 backups, .1/.2/.3 naming, synchronized writes). Do NOT duplicate a fragile hand-rolled rotation — mirror the proven one.
3. Gate persistence on UnifiedConfigManager (isTimingLogsEnabled or a dedicated developerOptions key). Off by default. When disabled, no file is opened or written.
4. Keep the existing 1 Hz sampling, the 60-sample in-memory ring, the on-demand client lifecycle, and PerformanceBridge unchanged — persistence is an additional sink, not a replacement.
5. Ensure the writer is closed/flushed cleanly when monitoring stops.

CONSTRAINTS — do NOT change: sampling interval, the on-demand start/stop driven by WebView client connect/disconnect, PerformanceBridge JS-facing methods, or the snapshot field set (you may add a timestamp). 

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles (./gradlew assembleDebug) and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

Rotation by size with a bounded number of backups (match DebugAppLogger style: ~5MB×3). Writing is gated by a toggle and off by default. Existing in-memory 60-sample history and PerformanceBridge behavior are unchanged. Build compiles. File appears and grows when enabled; nothing written when disabled.

title: Perf instrumentation: profile GPU/motion pipeline & persist metrics
description:
Developer logging is sufficient for debugging but under-instrumented for OPTIMIZATION. The system logs WHAT happened but rarely HOW LONG it took. There is no per-frame/per-stage timing in the GPU surveillance pipeline, PerformanceMonitor metrics are coarse (1 Hz) and ephemeral (60 in-memory samples, lost on disconnect), native motion/GPU code emits only init/error logs, and daemon startup timings cannot be correlated across processes (each measures relative to its own _startTime).

This epic groups four instrumentation improvements, ordered by leverage:
1. (highest) Per-stage timing in GpuSurveillancePipeline with rolling p50/p95.
2. Persist PerformanceMonitor snapshots to rotating CSV/JSONL.
3. Native nanoTime spans in motion pipeline + texture binder, flag-gated.
4. Shared epoch baseline so daemon startup timings align on one timeline.

See child tasks for detail. Background: existing logging stack = DaemonLogger.java (daemon, /data/local/tmp, 10MB×3), DebugAppLogger.kt (app, /storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/debug_app.log), 42 flags in DaemonLogConfig.java, runtime toggles in SettingsPrivacyFragment.kt backed by developerOptions in UnifiedConfigManager.kt (timingLogsEnabled, debugLogsEnabled). Startup timing already uses a logT('[STARTUP +Nms]') pattern in CameraDaemon/SentryDaemon/AccSentryDaemon/DaemonStartupManager gated on UnifiedConfigManager.isTimingLogsEnabled().

title: Add TFLite GPU kernel serialization (cache OpenCL kernels to disk)
description:
YoloDetector creates GpuDelegate() with no options (YoloDetector.kt:143), so the Adreno OpenCL backend recompiles all GPU kernels inside allocateTensors() on every daemon start (~3-5s cold start). Add GpuDelegate.Options.setSerializationParams(serializationDir, modelToken) so only the first boot pays the compile cost.

Requirements:
- Cache dir: /data/local/tmp/tflite_gpu_cache (shell-UID writable, survives reboot). Create if missing.
- modelToken MUST be a content hash of the model bytes + TFLite version string, so a re-exported model invalidates stale kernels. Do NOT hardcode a static token.
- Keep change inside the existing Tier-1 try/catch so serialization failure cannot break the NNAPI/CPU fallback chain.
- Log whether a cache hit occurred vs cold compile.
- OpenCL-only: silently no-ops on OpenGL ES backend; that is acceptable.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] GpuDelegate constructed with Options.setSerializationParams
- [ ] Token derived from model content hash, not static
- [ ] Cache dir created with safe fallback
- [ ] Build compiles (./gradlew assembleDebug)
- [ ] Fallback chain unchanged

Do not make mistakes. Read YoloDetector.kt fully before editing.
close_reason: Implemented GPU kernel serialization in YoloDetector.kt: GpuDelegateFactory.Options.setSerializationParams into /data/local/tmp/tflite_gpu_cache, token = SHA-256 content hash of model bytes + TFLite version. Wrapped in Tier-1 try/catch so failure cannot break NNAPI/CPU fallback; cache dir created with fallback; timing log distinguishes cache hit vs cold compile. Build compiles clean (no deprecation warning). Docs updated.

title: Create StartupFragment.kt — startup progress screen logic
description:
Create the Kotlin fragment that implements the startup progress screen logic.

**File to create:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/StartupFragment.kt`
**Package:** `net.bladewatch.app.ui.fragment`

This fragment is the first screen shown when the app opens. It observes daemon states and shows per-daemon startup progress. It blocks access to the rest of the app until all 3 core daemons are RUNNING, then auto-navigates to the dashboard.

**Dependencies — read these files fully before implementing:**
- Layout: `app/src/main/res/layout/fragment_startup.xml` (all view IDs are defined there)
- Nav action: `app/src/main/res/navigation/nav_graph.xml` — action ID `R.id.action_startupFragment_to_dashboardFragment`
- ViewModel: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/viewmodel/DaemonsViewModel.kt` — field `daemonStates: LiveData<Map<DaemonType, DaemonState>>`
- Models: `DaemonType.kt`, `DaemonStatus.kt`, `DaemonState.kt` in `com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/model/`
- Colors: `app/src/main/res/values/colors.xml` for color references

**Class-level fields:**
```kotlin
private val daemonsViewModel: DaemonsViewModel by activityViewModels()
private val handler = Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())
private val daemonStartedAtMs = mutableMapOf<DaemonType, Long>()
private val daemonCompletedAtMs = mutableMapOf<DaemonType, Long>()
private var fragmentCreatedAtMs = 0L
private var navigated = false
```

**View fields (bound in onViewCreated):**
```kotlin
private lateinit var tvStartupHeader: TextView
private lateinit var tvStartupElapsed: TextView
private lateinit var progressStartup: com.google.android.material.progressindicator.LinearProgressIndicator
private lateinit var btnContinueAnyway: com.google.android.material.button.MaterialButton
// Per-daemon: dot View, status TextView, elapsed TextView — store in maps keyed by DaemonType
private val statusDots = mutableMapOf<DaemonType, View>()
private val statusLabels = mutableMapOf<DaemonType, TextView>()
private val elapsedLabels = mutableMapOf<DaemonType, TextView>()
```

**onCreateView:** inflate R.layout.fragment_startup

**onViewCreated logic:**
1. `fragmentCreatedAtMs = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()`
2. Bind views: tvStartupHeader, tvStartupElapsed, progressStartup, btnContinueAnyway
3. Populate maps for each DaemonType:
   - CAMERA_DAEMON → R.id.statusDotCamera, R.id.tvCameraStatus, R.id.tvCameraElapsed
   - SENTRY_DAEMON → R.id.statusDotSentry, R.id.tvSentryStatus, R.id.tvSentryElapsed
   - ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON → R.id.statusDotAccSentry, R.id.tvAccSentryStatus, R.id.tvAccSentryElapsed
4. `btnContinueAnyway.setOnClickListener { navigateToDashboard() }`
5. Observe `daemonsViewModel.daemonStates`:
   - For each of the 3 core daemon types, call `updateDaemonRow(type, state)`
   - After updating all 3, check: if all 3 have status == RUNNING → call `onAllDaemonsReady()`
6. Start ticker: `handler.post(tickerRunnable)`
7. Show continue button after 120s: `handler.postDelayed({ if (!navigated) btnContinueAnyway.visibility = View.VISIBLE }, 120_000)`

**updateDaemonRow(type: DaemonType, state: DaemonState):**
- Record start time: if state.status == STARTING and daemonStartedAtMs[type] == null → `daemonStartedAtMs[type] = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()`
- Record complete time: if state.status == RUNNING and daemonCompletedAtMs[type] == null → `daemonCompletedAtMs[type] = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()`
- Update dot background resource:
  - STOPPED → R.drawable.status_dot_offline
  - STARTING → R.drawable.status_dot_starting
  - RUNNING → R.drawable.status_dot_online
  - ERROR / other → R.drawable.status_dot_offline (with setColorFilter for red, OR just use status_dot_offline — check what error drawable exists first)
- Update status label text + color:
  - STOPPED → "WAITING" + getColor(R.color.text_muted)
  - STARTING → "STARTING" + getColor(R.color.status_starting)
  - RUNNING → "RUNNING" + getColor(R.color.status_running)
  - ERROR → "ERROR" + getColor(R.color.status_error)
- Update elapsed label:
  - STOPPED → "—"
  - STARTING → live (ticker handles this)
  - RUNNING → "${((daemonCompletedAtMs[type]!! - (daemonStartedAtMs[type] ?: daemonCompletedAtMs[type]!!)) / 1000)}s"
  - ERROR → current elapsed or "—"

**tickerRunnable (runs every 1000ms while not navigated):**
```kotlin
private val tickerRunnable = object : Runnable {
    override fun run() {
        if (navigated) return
        val overallElapsed = (SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - fragmentCreatedAtMs) / 1000
        tvStartupElapsed.text = "${overallElapsed}s"
        // Update header text based on state
        val states = daemonsViewModel.daemonStates.value ?: emptyMap()
        val coreDaemons = listOf(DaemonType.CAMERA_DAEMON, DaemonType.SENTRY_DAEMON, DaemonType.ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON)
        tvStartupHeader.text = when {
            coreDaemons.all { states[it]?.status == DaemonStatus.RUNNING } -> "All systems ready"
            coreDaemons.any { states[it]?.status == DaemonStatus.STARTING } -> "Starting daemons..."
            else -> "Preparing system..."
        }
        // Update elapsed for STARTING daemons
        for (type in coreDaemons) {
            val startedAt = daemonStartedAtMs[type] ?: continue
            if (states[type]?.status == DaemonStatus.STARTING) {
                val elapsed = (SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - startedAt) / 1000
                elapsedLabels[type]?.text = "${elapsed}s"
            }
        }
        handler.postDelayed(this, 1000)
    }
}
```

**onAllDaemonsReady():**
```kotlin
private fun onAllDaemonsReady() {
    if (navigated) return
    progressStartup.visibility = View.GONE
    btnContinueAnyway.visibility = View.VISIBLE
    btnContinueAnyway.text = "Continue →"
    handler.postDelayed({ navigateToDashboard() }, 1500)
}
```

**navigateToDashboard():**
```kotlin
private fun navigateToDashboard() {
    if (navigated) return
    navigated = true
    try {
        findNavController().navigate(R.id.action_startupFragment_to_dashboardFragment)
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        // Fragment may have been detached — ignore
    }
}
```

**onDestroyView:**
```kotlin
override fun onDestroyView() {
    super.onDestroyView()
    handler.removeCallbacksAndMessages(null)
}
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] File compiles with no unresolved references
- [ ] Uses `activityViewModels()` (not `viewModels()`) so it shares the same DaemonsViewModel instance as MainActivity
- [ ] Observes daemonsViewModel.daemonStates and updates all 3 daemon rows on each emission
- [ ] Per-daemon elapsed: "—" while STOPPED, live ticking Xs while STARTING, frozen Xs when RUNNING
- [ ] Auto-navigates to dashboard 1.5s after all 3 core daemons reach RUNNING
- [ ] "Continue anyway" button appears at 120s if not yet navigated
- [ ] Handler cleared in onDestroyView to prevent leaks
- [ ] Project builds: `./gradlew assembleDebug`

Do not make mistakes. Read all referenced files fully before writing. Check that R.color and R.drawable references exist before using them. Do not use R.id values that aren't defined in fragment_startup.xml. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Perf: replace getAllLite() full table scan with GROUP BY SQL for stats/dates aggregation
description:
## Problem
RecordingsDatabase.getAllLite() (line 304) fetches every row (filename, type, size_bytes, timestamp_ms) into a List<JSONObject> in Java heap. Its callers — datesFromDb() and aggregateStatsFromDb() in RecordingsApiHandler — iterate this full list in Java to compute counts, sums, and date strings. With 600+ recordings this allocates hundreds of JSONObject instances and holds the synchronized RecordingsDatabase monitor for the full scan duration, blocking concurrent live-indexing writes from the recorder.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/RecordingsDatabase.java
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/RecordingsApiHandler.java (datesFromDb, aggregateStatsFromDb callers)

## Fix approach
Replace getAllLite() with two purpose-built SQL methods:

1. getStatsByType() — returns a Map<String, long[]> keyed by type ('normal', 'sentry', 'proximity'), each value being [count, totalSizeBytes]:
   SQL: SELECT type, COUNT(*), SUM(size_bytes) FROM recordings GROUP BY type
   Returns 3 rows max regardless of table size.

2. getDistinctDates() — returns distinct YYYY-MM-DD date strings and per-date sentry presence:
   SQL: SELECT DISTINCT FORMATDATETIME(DATEADD('MILLISECOND', timestamp_ms, TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00'), 'yyyy-MM-dd') as dt, MAX(CASE WHEN type='sentry' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as has_sentry FROM recordings GROUP BY dt ORDER BY dt DESC
   (H2 supports FORMATDATETIME and DATEADD — verify syntax against H2 2.2.224 docs)
