title: Fix: storage stats use stale DB size_bytes instead of live file.length()
description:
## Problem
RecordingsApiHandler.aggregateStatsFromDb() reads the size_bytes column stored in the recordings DB table to compute storage totals. This value is set at index time and never updated unless a reconcile runs. If a file is corrupted or partially overwritten after indexing (e.g. SD card write error on the BYD head unit), the stored size_bytes is stale and the storage usage bar shows an incorrect total until the user manually runs 'Sync Database'.

The old filesystem fallback path (aggregateStatsFromFilesystem) always called file.length() live, so this is a regression specific to the new DB-first read path.

## Relevant code
- RecordingsApiHandler.java: aggregateStatsFromDb() — find the method that reads from getAllLite() and sums 'size' fields
- RecordingsDatabase.java: getAllLite() returns size_bytes column

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/RecordingsApiHandler.java

## Fix approach
In aggregateStatsFromDb(), for each row where the 'path' field is set, call new File(path).length() and use that value instead of the stored size. If the file no longer exists (length returns 0), use the stored size_bytes as a fallback (so stats don't go to zero for files momentarily unavailable). Add a comment explaining the live-vs-cached tradeoff.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the DB schema or the upsert path — size_bytes is still useful for reconcile change-detection
- This change only affects the stats aggregation, not the per-recording JSON returned by getRecordings()

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After corrupting a file's size on disk (truncate), GET /api/recordings/stats shows the actual size, not the stale DB value
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read the relevant sections of RecordingsApiHandler.java before editing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: aggregateForStats() calls File.length() per path and uses live size if non-zero, falling back to stored size_bytes if file is temporarily unavailable.

title: Live view H.264 pixelation/macroblock artifacts in camera feed
description:
The native live view (LiveStreamClient.kt) shows intermittent H.264 decode corruption: a mosaic/macroblock band along the bottom of the frame plus scattered colored macroblocks (blue/purple/yellow/cyan). The top of the frame decodes cleanly. Observed on the BYD head unit (192.168.0.251) front camera after the IPC-token auth fix made live view work again (2026-06-07).

Likely cause: dropped frames. In app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/liveview/LiveStreamClient.kt around lines 136-143, when MediaCodec.dequeueInputBuffer() returns <0 (no free input buffer within INPUT_TIMEOUT_US=10ms) the incoming H.264 frame is SILENTLY DROPPED (the queueInputBuffer is inside the inputIdx>=0 branch with no else). Dropping a P-frame corrupts all subsequent frames until the next IDR keyframe, which matches the observed progressive/partial corruption. Contributing factors to investigate: (1) encoder keyframe/IDR interval on the daemon side (HttpServer.enableStreaming / pipeline) — a long GOP makes corruption persist; (2) WebSocket read backpressure (READ_TIMEOUT_MS, BufferedInputStream); (3) decoder resolution: queryStreamDimensions() defaults to 640x480 if /api/stream/quality fails — verify it matches the actual encoder resolution (fisheye is ~square), a stride/height mismatch can also cause bottom-band garbage.

Suggested approach: (a) handle the dropped-input-buffer case (retry/block briefly or request a keyframe on drop); (b) ensure the encoder emits frequent IDR frames or expose a 'request keyframe' command the client calls on decode error; (c) confirm decoder dimensions match the stream. Reproduce by opening Live view and observing the bottom of the frame.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Root cause of the macroblock corruption identified and confirmed (frame drop vs resolution mismatch vs GOP length).
- [ ] Fix implemented so the live feed renders without persistent macroblock corruption under normal load.
- [ ] Verified on-device: open Live view, observe a clean feed for >30s across at least Front and one other direction.
- [ ] No regression to live-view startup latency or auth.

Do not make mistakes. Read LiveStreamClient.kt and the daemon-side streaming encoder fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and test on the head unit before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-06-07): WebSocket fragmentation not reassembled on the client. Server (HttpServer.streamH264ToWebSocket / sendWebSocketBinaryFrame, MAX_WS_FRAME_SIZE=32768) splits any H.264 access unit >32KB into a binary frame (opcode 0x2, FIN=0) + continuation frames (opcode 0x0). Client LiveStreamClient.runStream only handled OPCODE_BINARY/CLOSE/PING and ignored the FIN bit, so continuation frames were dropped and every unit >32KB was truncated to its first 32KB -> macroblock corruption (keyframes + busy P-frames exceed 32KB). FIX APPLIED: WsFrame now carries fin; readWsFrame captures FIN; runStream reassembles binary+continuation fragments until FIN before feeding the decoder (LiveViewModels.kt, LiveStreamClient.kt). Pending on-device verification.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on-device (2026-06-07). Root cause: client did not reassemble fragmented WebSocket messages, truncating every H.264 access unit >32KB to its first 32KB. Fix: WsFrame carries fin; readWsFrame captures the FIN bit; runStream reassembles OPCODE_BINARY + OPCODE_CONTINUATION fragments until FIN before feeding the decoder. Live view now renders clean top-to-bottom with no macroblock corruption across multiple captures and view changes.

title: Add shared-secret authentication to TcpCommandServer (port 19876)
description:
## Problem
TcpCommandServer binds to 127.0.0.1:19876 and processes privileged commands (start/stop cameras, enable/disable surveillance, daemon shutdown, live frame capture) with ZERO authentication. Any Android app on the BYD head unit can connect and issue any command. The daemon runs as shell UID (2000), so commands have elevated access.

## Exploit
A malicious app on the car's head unit connects to 127.0.0.1:19876, sends {"cmd": "disableSurveillance"}, and sentry mode is silently disabled before a break-in.

## File
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java
  - handleClient() at ~line 84: accepts and processes commands with no auth check

## Fix Approach
Option A (recommended): Shared secret token file
1. Daemon generates a random 32-char alphanumeric token at startup using SecureRandom.
2. Writes it to /data/data/net.bladewatch.app/files/ipc_token (chmod 600, shell UID owner) — or a shell-UID-only path.
3. TcpCommandServer requires the first JSON message to contain {"token": "<value>"} before processing any commands; reject and close connection if missing or wrong.
4. DaemonHttpClient reads the token file before connecting.

Option B: Unix domain socket
Move the IPC to a Unix socket at /data/data/net.bladewatch.app/ipc.sock — Android enforces socket ownership via filesystem permissions, restricting access to the app UID. More secure but requires changes to both ends.

## Constraints
- DaemonHttpClient is the only expected caller — read it to understand the client side
- The fix must not break existing daemon startup flow
- Do NOT break the health check ping used by DaemonKeepaliveService

## Files to Read First
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java (full)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/client/DaemonHttpClient.java (or similar — find the TCP client)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TcpCommandServer rejects connections that don't provide the correct token
- [ ] DaemonHttpClient reads and sends the token
- [ ] Existing IPC commands still work end-to-end
- [ ] ./gradlew test passes

Do not make mistakes. Read both the server and client files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles. If the client-side location is unclear, search for 127.0.0.1:19876 references. Stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Add payload size guard to LiveStreamClient.readWsFrame() — prevent overflow crash
description:
## Problem

LiveStreamClient.readWsFrame() reads a 64-bit payload length from the WebSocket frame header but immediately casts it to Int without bounds checking.

**File:** app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/liveview/LiveStreamClient.kt  
**Line 259:** `val payload = ByteArray(payloadLen.toInt())`

If payloadLen > Int.MAX_VALUE (2,147,483,647 = ~2GB), payloadLen.toInt() overflows to a negative number and ByteArray(negative) throws NegativeArraySizeException. The outer catch(Throwable) catches it and causes an unexpected stream disconnect. For normal H.264 video frames this never happens in practice, but it's a correctness bug.

## Fix

Add a guard before the allocation (after line 258):
```kotlin
if (payloadLen > 4 * 1024 * 1024L) {  // 4MB max — H.264 frames are never this large
    publish(LiveStreamStatus.Error("Frame too large: ${payloadLen}"))
    return null
}
val payload = ByteArray(payloadLen.toInt())
```

The publish() call in readWsFrame would require passing the callback or returning a special sentinel. Alternatively, throw an IOException here which is caught by the existing catch block.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] payloadLen > 4MB causes a clean error state rather than an integer overflow
- [ ] Normal H.264 frames (typically < 200KB) are unaffected
- [ ] Build passes (./gradlew assembleDebug)

Do not make mistakes. Read LiveStreamClient.kt fully before editing.
close_reason: Closed

title: fix: TripsController DNA bar fill uses hardcoded 1000px causing overflow on BYD head unit
description:
## Context
buildDnaBar() in TripsController.kt line 430 uses (fraction * 1000).toInt() as the pixel width of the fill View inside a FrameLayout. This hardcodes an absolute 1000px width as a proxy for 100% fill. On the BYD head unit at density ~2.0 (1280x720), the barBg container resolves to ~896px after label (dp(130)=260px), score label (~60px), and card padding (~64px). ## File
app/src/main/java/net/bladewatch/app/ui/fragment/trips/TripsController.kt
buildDnaBar() approximately lines 414-440
The fill View with FrameLayout.LayoutParams((fraction * 1000).toInt(), MATCH_PARENT) around line 430.

## What to do
Replace the fixed-pixel approach with a ViewTreeObserver measurement after the barBg is laid out:
  val fill = View(context).apply {
      background = pillBackground(Color.parseColor('#4CAF50'))
      layoutParams = FrameLayout.LayoutParams(0, ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT)
  }
  barBg.addView(fill)
  barBg.viewTreeObserver.addOnGlobalLayoutListener(object : android.view.ViewTreeObserver.OnGlobalLayoutListener {
      override fun onGlobalLayout() {
          barBg.viewTreeObserver.removeOnGlobalLayoutListener(this)
          fill.layoutParams = FrameLayout.LayoutParams(
              (fraction * barBg.width).toInt(),

title: Fix double loadData() on first show in RecordingSettings, Trips, SurveillanceSettings controllers
description:
## Problem

Three native controllers call loadData() in both init {} and onResume(), causing two concurrent HTTP requests every time the user navigates to these screens for the first time.

**Files:**
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/recording/RecordingSettingsController.kt — line 39 (init) and line 42 (onResume)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/trips/TripsController.kt — lines 55 and 60
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsController.kt — lines 64 and 68

The Fragment lifecycle is: onCreateView (constructor runs → init → loadData #1) → onResume (loadData #2). The second call arrives while the first may still be in-flight, causing a flash of 'Loading…' over already-loaded content.

## Fix

Add a flag to track whether the initial load has completed. In each controller:
```kotlin
private var loadedOnce = false

fun onResume() { if (loadedOnce) loadData() }

private fun loadData() {
    // existing impl...
    // at the end of the root.post { ... } completion block:
    loadedOnce = true
}
```

Apply the same fix to all three controllers: RecordingSettingsController, TripsController, SurveillanceSettingsController.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Navigating to Recording Settings, Trips, or Surveillance Settings for the first time triggers exactly one HTTP request
- [ ] Subsequent navigations (back then forward) still refresh data via onResume
- [ ] Build passes (./gradlew assembleDebug)
- [ ] Fix applied to all three controllers

title: VehicleController: show error state when daemon is unreachable after 3 failed polls
description:
## Problem

VehicleController shows 'Checking…' indefinitely when the CameraDaemon is not reachable. The status card lock text is set to 'Checking…' at init and only updated when fetchState() returns a non-null result. If the daemon is down (normal during the 45-second startup delay), the user has no indication that something is wrong.

**File:** app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt  
**Lines 643-658:** startPolling() — the scheduleAtFixedRate block just returns early on null (line 654), never updating the UI

## Fix

Add a consecutive-failure counter in startPolling():
```kotlin
var failCount = 0
sched.scheduleAtFixedRate({
    if (!running.get()) { sched.shutdownNow(); return@scheduleAtFixedRate }
    val state = client.fetchState()
    if (state == null) {
        failCount++
        if (failCount >= 3) root.post { 
            if (running.get()) showErrorState("Vehicle data unavailable. Check daemon status.") 
        }
        return@scheduleAtFixedRate
    }
    failCount = 0
    vehicleState = state.copy(chargeCap = vehicleState.chargeCap)
    root.post { if (running.get()) applyStateToViews() }
}, 0, 3, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
```

Add a showErrorState() that updates the status card text to the error message and the dot to gray.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After 3 consecutive failed fetchState() calls (~9 seconds), the status card shows an error message
- [ ] When fetchState() succeeds again, the error state clears and normal state resumes
- [ ] Lock status dot turns gray during error state
- [ ] No crash if the daemon recovers after showing the error
- [ ] Build passes (./gradlew assembleDebug)

Do not make mistakes. Read VehicleController.kt fully before editing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.

title: SetRecordingMode RPC returns success=true on invalid mode (silent no-op)
description:
## Problem
SettingsService.SetRecordingMode (added in BladeWatch-pg0s) calls CameraDaemon.setRecordingMode(mode), which does Mode.valueOf(mode.toUpperCase()) and SWALLOWS IllegalArgumentException for unknown modes (CameraDaemon.java:2336 logs "Invalid recording mode" and returns). The Connect impl handleSetRecordingMode then still returns {success:true, mode}. So an invalid mode string is a silent no-op reported as success.

Low severity today: the UI only sends valid enum values (selectedMode.value), and this matches the old REST behavior. But it is a latent correctness gap.

## Files
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/SettingsServiceImpl.java (handleSetRecordingMode, ~line 101)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java (setRecordingMode, ~line 2325)

## Steps
1. Make setRecordingMode signal failure for an invalid mode (e.g. return boolean, or expose a validated setter / check against RecordingModeManager.Mode values), without breaking other callers.
2. In handleSetRecordingMode, validate the mode (against the Mode enum) and return success=false with error="invalid_mode: <mode>" (or throw ConnectException invalid_argument) when it does not apply.
3. Keep success=true only when the mode was actually applied.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SetRecordingMode with a bogus mode returns success=false (or invalid_argument), not success=true.
- [ ] SetRecordingMode with a valid mode still applies and returns success=true.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes; add a small unit test if feasible.

Do not make mistakes. Read both files fully and check all callers of CameraDaemon.setRecordingMode before changing its signature. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Added enum validation in SettingsServiceImpl.handleSetRecordingMode before calling CameraDaemon — invalid mode now throws ConnectException(invalid_argument) instead of silently returning success=true. compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes.

title: Connect parity STRUCTURAL: Surveillance status/heatmap/filterlog shapes
description:
## Problem
SurveillanceService Connect<->REST mismatches that json_name cannot cleanly fix. Audited under BladeWatch-s4k: GetSurveillanceConfigResponse fully MATCHES (no change needed); GetSnapshotResponse matches via captureBytes. The rest are structural/ambiguous.

Background: daemon ships REST JSON verbatim; client parses with JsonFormat.ignoringUnknownFields(). See epic BladeWatch-48b.

## Structural mismatches
1. GetSurveillanceStatusResponse (surveillance.proto ~101): proto = {pipeline_running, surveillance_active, active_cameras, error}. CameraDaemon.getSurveillanceStatus() (~2365) emits {initialized, enabled, active(=gpuPipeline.isRunning), recording, frameCount, ... 50+ keys}. AMBIGUOUS mapping: 'active'=pipeline isRunning, 'enabled'=surveillanceEnabled — so which maps to pipeline_running vs surveillance_active needs the original intent. active_cameras has NO emitter. Decide the intended field semantics, then either redesign the proto status message to the fields the client actually needs (with json_name) or adjust the emitter. Verify what SurveillanceSettingsClient.kt / Angular consume.
2. GetHeatmapResponse (surveillance.proto ~126): proto declares image_jpeg (bytes); SurveillanceApiHandler.sendHeatmap (~1091) emits a heatmap GRID structure {gridCols,gridRows,viewMode,quadrants[...]} — NOT a JPEG. Decide: model the grid in proto OR rename. (GetSnapshotResponse.image_jpeg is fine via Connect captureBytes.)
3. FilterLogEntry / GetFilterLogResponse (surveillance.proto ~144-152): proto FilterLogEntry = {timestamp_ms, reason, details}; emitter returns an array of PLAIN STRINGS (sentry.getFilterLogEntries()), plus an extra 'count'. Decide: emit structured objects OR model entries as repeated string.

## Constraints
- Do NOT break web UI (REST keys) or Angular TS client. Align proto to actual emitted JSON where possible; if restructuring, regenerate stubs (buf) and update Kotlin/TS consumers so the build compiles.
- Regenerate via ./gradlew generateConnectProtos; verify ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each of the 3 areas resolved with a documented decision (esp. the status field-semantics).
- [ ] Stubs regenerated; consumers updated; compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes.

Do not make mistakes. Read surveillance.proto, CameraDaemon.getSurveillanceStatus(), SurveillanceApiHandler.sendHeatmap/sendFilterLog, and the consumers fully before editing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.

or with json_name to match an existing key) OR remove the unused proto field.

Read the epic background for the general mechanism.

1. BatteryInfo.is_charging (system.proto) — BatteryMonitor.getBatteryInfo() does not emit isCharging.
2. BatteryInfo.status_string (system.proto) — not emitted by getBatteryInfo().

4. ListModelsResponse.success (system.proto) — ModelsApiHandler list response has no success wrapper.
5. PreviewCleanupFile.age_hours — handled in the PreviewCleanup task; SKIP here to avoid overlap.

    existing emitted key. For success on list endpoints, add response wrapper {"success":true,...}

title: Cleanup: fix dead code in ConnectHandlerUtil and ConnectDispatcher
description:
## Dead code to fix

Three distinct dead-code issues in the Connect layer:

### 1. ConnectDispatcher.sendConnectSuccess() — null guard on extraHeaders (always non-null)
File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java

In sendConnectSuccess(), the check 'if (extraHeaders != null)' is always true because ConnectResponse's constructor guarantees extraHeaders is always Collections.emptyList() or Collections.unmodifiableList(...), never null. Remove the null check; just iterate directly.

### 2. ConnectHandlerUtil.requireString() — v == null check is dead (line 176)
File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java

'JSONObject.getString(field)' either returns a non-null String or throws JSONException. It cannot return null. The '|| v == null' branch is unreachable and misleads readers. Remove the v == null check:
  if (v.isEmpty()) throw new Exception("empty");

### 3. ConnectHandlerUtil.captureString() — unnecessary parse+serialize round-trip
File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java (line 150-152)

captureString() currently calls capture() (which parses body as JSONObject) then calls .toString() (re-serializes). This is a pointless round-trip. Worse, it silently transforms the body: array-bodied responses get wrapped as {"items":[...]}, and non-JSON bodies become "{}". captureString should directly call captureRaw() and decode the body bytes to a UTF-8 string:

  public static ConnectResponse captureString(HandlerInvoker invoker) throws ConnectException {
      RawCapture raw = captureRaw(invoker);
      String body = new String(raw.bodyBytes, StandardCharsets.UTF_8).trim();
      if (body.isEmpty()) body = "{}";
      return ConnectResponse.of(body);
  }

NOTE: This change also means captureString will stop silently swallowing HTTP errors if issue BladeWatch-2oq is fixed first (which adds status checking to captureRaw/the capture helpers). Coordinate with BladeWatch-2oq.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ConnectDispatcher: null guard on extraHeaders removed
- [ ] ConnectHandlerUtil: v == null check in requireString removed
- [ ] ConnectHandlerUtil: captureString uses captureRaw directly, no round-trip through JSONObject
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read the relevant files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: LiveStreamClient enableStream()/setViewMode() swallow ConnectRPC failures before opening WebSocket
description:

title: ConnectDispatcher/capture leak raw exception messages to client
description:
Unhandled exceptions surface their raw message (and possibly internal paths) to the Connect client, which is risky for a tunnel-exposed daemon.

title: ConnectDispatcher maps all ConnectException codes to HTTP 400 regardless of semantic code
description:
All Connect errors are sent with HTTP 400, ignoring the actual semantic code, so unavailable/not_found/unauthenticated are mis-delivered and Connect clients mis-handle retries.

DETAIL: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java (~line 109) catch block always calls sendConnectError(out, 400, ...) regardless of e.getCode(). Per the Connect protocol the HTTP status must reflect the code (invalid_argument->400, unauthenticated->401, not_found->404, unavailable->503, internal->500, etc.). E.g. TripsServiceImpl throws ConnectException('unavailable','Trip analytics not initialized') — a strict Connect client (or proxy retry logic) keying off HTTP status treats the 'unavailable' as a permanent 400 client error and won't retry.

FIX: Add a code->HTTP-status mapping and use it in sendConnectError. This pairs with the TripsServiceImpl _status task — once errors carry correct codes, the status mapping makes them correct end-to-end.

FILES: server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java, server/connect/ConnectException.java.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] Each Connect error code maps to its correct HTTP status (verify unavailable->503, not_found->404, unauthenticated->401, invalid_argument->400, internal->500).
- [ ] The Connect error body still carries the code+message.

title: AuthService/Login not in AuthMiddleware PUBLIC_PATHS: Connect login unreachable when unauthenticated (latent)

There is a loopback bypass but it is BuildConfig.DEBUG-only and a LAN/tunnel browser request is not loopback. The current web login form (login.html) posts to REST /auth/token (public), so this is latent — but AuthServiceClient.kt already references the Connect endpoint.

title: Shared epoch baseline so daemon startup timings align on one timeline
description:
GOAL: Today each daemon's startup timing is measured relative to its OWN _startTime, so cross-process events cannot be lined up on one timeline. Add a shared epoch baseline so all [STARTUP +Nms] logs can be correlated.

CONTEXT / FILES TO READ FULLY FIRST:
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java (logT pattern + _startTime, ~lines 82-87, 244)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/SentryDaemon.java (logT ~lines 36-41)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/AccSentryDaemon.java (logT ~lines 106-111)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/DaemonStartupManager.kt (logT/elapsed ~lines 23-28; orchestrates staggered launches at 45s/60s/90s)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/DaemonLauncher.kt (cameraLaunchStartMs etc, ~lines 50-63) — DaemonStartupManager already records absolute launch-start timestamps; this is the natural shared anchor
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt (isTimingLogsEnabled)

APPROACH OPTIONS (pick the simplest that works; check files before deciding):
A. Include the absolute epoch (System.currentTimeMillis()) in each logT line in addition to the relative offset, so any two daemons' lines can be merged and sorted by absolute time. This is the least invasive and likely sufficient.
B. Write a shared boot/epoch anchor to a small file under /data/local/tmp (e.g. bladewatch_boot_epoch) when DaemonStartupManager begins, and have each daemon log its offset relative to that shared anchor.

STEPS:
1. Decide between A and B (prefer A unless a single normalized offset is specifically wanted). 
2. Modify the logT helpers in CameraDaemon, SentryDaemon, AccSentryDaemon, and DaemonStartupManager so each emitted line carries the absolute epoch (or shared-anchor offset). Keep the existing relative '+Nms' value too.
3. Keep all changes gated behind UnifiedConfigManager.isTimingLogsEnabled() exactly as today.

CONSTRAINTS — do NOT change: the staggered startup timing (45s/60s/90s), daemon launch order, or any non-logging behavior. Observability only.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Fix: buildBasicTrip() produces distanceKm=0.0 for single-sample telemetry files
description:
## Problem
TripAnalyticsManager.buildBasicTrip() (line 309) is called during reconcileTrips() to reconstruct minimal trip records from orphan .jsonl.gz telemetry files. When a telemetry file contains exactly one sample, the GPS haversine loop runs once: hasLast is false on the only iteration, so haversineKm() is never called, and distanceKm stays 0.0. The stored trip record shows 0 km distance even if the sample has valid GPS coordinates, producing a visibly wrong entry in the trips list.

## Relevant code
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/trips/TripAnalyticsManager.java lines 309–347 (buildBasicTrip)

More importantly, skip inserting single-sample trips entirely in reconcileTrips() (line 281) since they represent incomplete or corrupt telemetry files — a trip with 1 telemetry sample is not a real trip. Add a log line: 'Skipping single-sample telemetry file: ' + f.getName().

## Constraints

- Do NOT delete the telemetry .jsonl.gz file on disk — only skip the DB insert

title: Cleanup: deduplicate date-parsing logic between scanDirectory() and dateRangeMs()
description:

  long[] range = dateRangeMs(dateFilter);
  long filterStart = range[0];
  long filterEnd = range[1];
Remove the inner try/catch that was wrapping the inline block — dateRangeMs() already catches and handles exceptions.

title: fix: PerformanceController optString returns empty string not null when clientId missing
description:
## Context

  clientId = connectResp?.optString('clientId')
To:

title: Cleanup: make reconnect() synchronized or mark connection field volatile
description:
## Problem
RecordingsDatabase.reconnect() (line 116) writes to connection and isInitialized without holding the synchronized monitor. All current callers are inside synchronized methods so there is no live data race today, but connection is a plain (non-volatile) field. Under the Java Memory Model, a thread that calls isAvailable() (which IS synchronized) is guaranteed to see the latest values written by other synchronized callers. However, if reconnect() were ever called from an unsynchronized context in future, a reader could observe isInitialized=true with a stale null connection reference.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/RecordingsDatabase.java

## Fix
Add the synchronized modifier to reconnect() — it is a private method and all its callers already hold the monitor, so this is a no-op performance-wise but makes the contract explicit and prevents future callers from bypassing the lock. Alternatively, declare connection as volatile (matching the existing volatile isInitialized field).

Preferred: add synchronized to reconnect().

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the public API surface of RecordingsDatabase
- Do NOT add synchronized to a method that could introduce deadlock — reconnect() only acquires the instance monitor, which is the same monitor its callers hold (re-entrant, safe in Java)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] reconnect() is declared synchronized
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

This is a one-line change. Do not make mistakes.
close_reason: Added synchronized modifier to reconnect() in RecordingsDatabase.java. All callers already hold the instance monitor (re-entrant, no deadlock).
